title.zh: 卷六十七 列傳第十七: 李靖 李勣
title.en: Volume 67 Biographies 17: Li Jing, Li Ji
title.raw: 卷六十七 列傳第十七: 李靖 李勣 Volume 67 Biographies 17: Li Jing, Li Ji

sentences.zh: 李靖 客師 令問 彥芳

translations.literal: Li Jing; Keshe; Lingwen; Yanfang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing — with sections on Keshe, Lingwen, and Yanfang.

sentences.zh: 李勣 孫敬業

translations.literal: Li Ji; Sun Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji — with a section on Sun Jingye.

sentences.zh: 李靖，本名藥師，雍州三原人也。

translations.literal: Li Jing, original name Yaoshi, was a native of Sanyuan in Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, whose original name was Yaoshi, came from Sanyuan in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 祖崇義，後魏殷州刺史、永康公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chongyi was Governor of Yin Prefecture under the Later Wei and Duke of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chongyi had served as Governor of Yin Prefecture under the Later Wei and held the title Duke of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 父詮，隋趙郡守。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Administrator of Zhao Commandery under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan had been Administrator of Zhao Commandery in Sui times.

sentences.zh: 靖姿貌瑰偉，少有文武材略，每謂所親曰：「大丈夫若遇主逢時，必當立功立事，以取富貴。

translations.literal: Jing was striking in stature and appearance, and from youth possessed talent in both civil and military affairs; he often told those close to him, "If a great man meets his lord and his time, he must surely achieve merit and establish deeds to gain wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was imposing in build and bearing and showed civil and military ability from an early age. He often told those close to him, "When a man of stature finds his sovereign and his moment, he must win merit and make his mark to earn wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 」其舅韓擒虎，號為名將，每與論兵，未嘗不稱善，撫之曰：「可與論孫、吳之術者，惟斯人矣。

translations.literal: " His maternal uncle Han Qinhu, renowned as a famous general, whenever he discussed warfare with him never failed to praise him well, and stroking him said, "The only one with whom one may discuss the arts of Sun and Wu is this man.
translations.idiomatic: " His uncle by marriage, Han Qinhu, a general of celebrated name, would discuss warfare with him and unfailingly speak well of him, patting his shoulder and saying, "Of all those with whom one could discuss the strategies of Sunzi and Wuzi, this is the man.

sentences.zh: 」初仕隋為長安縣功曹，後歷駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: " At first he entered Sui service as Clerk of Records in Chang'an County, and later served successively as Vice Director in the Department of Imperial Transport.
translations.idiomatic: " He first entered Sui service as records clerk in Chang'an County and later rose to vice director in the imperial transport office.

sentences.zh: 左僕射楊素、吏部尚書牛弘皆善之。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Yang Su and Minister of Personnel Niu Hong both treated him favorably.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Vice Director Yang Su and the Minister of Personnel Niu Hong both took a liking to him.

sentences.zh: 素嘗拊其床謂靖曰：「卿終當坐此。

translations.literal: Su once patted his couch and said to Jing, "You will in the end sit here.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su once patted his own seat and told Jing, "You will one day sit in this place.

sentences.zh: 」大業末，累除馬邑郡丞。

translations.literal: " At the end of the Daye reign he was repeatedly appointed and removed as Assistant Magistrate of Mayi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " Toward the end of the Daye era he was appointed, after several promotions, assistant magistrate of Mayi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 會高祖擊突厥於塞外，靖察高祖，知有四方之志，因自鎖上變，將詣江都，至長安，道塞不通而止。

translations.literal: It happened that Gaozu was attacking the Turks beyond the frontier; Jing observed Gaozu and knew he harbored ambitions for the four quarters, and therefore chained himself to present a memorial of accusation, intending to go to Jiangdu; when he reached Chang'an the roads were blocked and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was campaigning against the Turks beyond the passes, Jing sized him up and saw that he harbored empire-wide ambitions. Jing therefore put himself in chains and prepared a denunciation to carry to the Sui emperor at Jiangdu, but when he reached Chang'an the roads were blocked and he went no farther.

sentences.zh: 高祖克京城，執靖將斬之，靖大呼曰：「公起義兵，本為天下除暴亂，不欲就大事，而以私怨斬壯士乎！

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the capital, he seized Jing and was about to execute him; Jing cried out loudly, "Your Lordship raised righteous troops originally to remove violence and disorder for the realm — do you not wish to accomplish the great enterprise, yet would kill a stalwart soldier over a private grudge!
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the capital he seized Jing and was about to execute him. Jing shouted, "You raised your army to rid the realm of tyranny and chaos — will you abandon the great cause and kill a able man over a private grievance?

sentences.zh: 」高祖壯其言，太宗又固請，遂舍之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu was impressed by his words, and Taizong also pressed his request firmly, so he released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu was struck by his boldness, and Taizong pleaded insistently on his behalf, so he was spared.

sentences.zh: 太宗尋召入幕府。

translations.literal: Taizong soon summoned him into his staff headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong soon brought him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，從討王世充，以功授開府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude he followed in the campaign against Wang Shichong and, for merit, was granted the title of Champion.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 3 he took part in the campaign against Wang Shichong and, for his service, was made a Champion of the state.

sentences.zh: 時蕭銑據荊州，遣靖安輯之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Xian held Jingzhou, and Jing was sent to pacify and settle the region.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian then held Jingzhou, and Jing was dispatched to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 輕騎至金州，遇蠻賊數萬，屯聚山谷。

translations.literal: With light cavalry he reached Jin Prefecture and encountered tens of thousands of barbarian bandits encamped in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Riding with a light force he reached Jin Prefecture and found tens of thousands of tribal raiders massed in the mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 廬江王瑗討之，數為所敗。

translations.literal: Prince of Lujiang Yuan attacked them but was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lujiang, Yuan, had attacked them but had been beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 靖與瑗設謀擊之，多所克獲。

translations.literal: Jing and Yuan devised a plan to strike them and took many captives and spoils.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Yuan laid a plan together and struck them, winning many victories and much booty.

sentences.zh: 既至硤州，阻蕭銑，久不得進。

translations.literal: When he had reached Xia Prefecture he was blocked by Xiao Xian and for a long time could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Xia Prefecture he was blocked by Xiao Xian and could not advance for a long time.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒其遲留，陰敕硤州都督許紹斬之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was angry at his delay and secretly ordered the Commissioner of Xia Prefecture, Xu Shao, to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was furious at the delay and secretly ordered the commissioner of Xia Prefecture, Xu Shao, to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 紹惜其才，為之請命，於是獲免。

translations.literal: Shao valued his talent and pleaded for his life on his behalf, and thus he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao valued his ability and pleaded for his life, and so he was spared.

sentences.zh: 會開州蠻首冉肇則反，率眾寇夔州，趙郡王孝恭與戰，不利。

translations.literal: It happened that the barbarian chieftain of Kai Prefecture, Ran Zhaize, rebelled and led his followers to raid Qie Prefecture; the Prince of Zhao Commandery, Xiaogong, fought him but fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: About then the tribal leader of Kai Prefecture, Ran Zhaize, rebelled and led his followers against Qie Prefecture. The Prince of Zhao Commandery, Xiaogong, met him in battle but fared badly.

sentences.zh: 靖率兵八百，襲破其營，後又要險設伏，臨陣斬肇則，俘獲五千餘人。

translations.literal: Jing led eight hundred troops, raided and broke his camp, and later again seized a defile to set an ambush, beheading Zhaize in battle and capturing more than five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led eight hundred men in a surprise attack that broke their camp. Later he laid an ambush in difficult terrain, slew Zhaize in the fighting, and took more than five thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚悅，謂公卿曰：「朕聞使功不如使過，李靖果展其效。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and said to the ministers, "I have heard that employing merit is not as good as employing fault — Li Jing has indeed displayed his effect.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and told his ministers, "They say it is better to use a man's fault than his merit — Li Jing has proved it.

sentences.zh: 」因降璽書勞曰：「卿竭誠盡力，功效特彰。

translations.literal: " He therefore issued an imperial letter of commendation saying, "You have exhausted sincerity and exerted all strength; your achievements are especially manifest.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent down an imperial letter of praise: "You have given your utmost loyalty and effort, and your achievements stand out.

sentences.zh: 遠覽至誠，極以嘉賞，勿憂富貴也。

translations.literal: Viewing from afar your utmost sincerity, I am extremely pleased to reward you — do not worry about wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Reading your devotion from afar, I reward you most highly — have no fear for your fortune and rank.

sentences.zh: 」又手敕靖曰：「既往不咎，舊事吾久忘之矣。

translations.literal: " He also personally wrote an edict to Jing saying, "What is past is not blamed; the old matter I have long forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote Jing a personal edict: "The past is not held against you — I have long forgotten the old affair.

sentences.zh: 」四年，靖又陳十策以圖蕭銑。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year Jing again presented ten stratagems for taking Xiao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " In year 4 Jing submitted ten stratagems for bringing down Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 高祖從之，授靖行軍總管，兼攝孝恭行軍長史。

translations.literal: Gaozu followed them and appointed Jing Campaign Commander, concurrently acting as Campaign Chief Clerk for Xiaogong.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu accepted the plan and made Jing campaign commander, with concurrent duty as chief clerk on Xiaogong's staff.

sentences.zh: 高祖以孝恭未更戎旅，三軍之任，一以委靖。

translations.literal: Because Gaozu considered that Xiaogong had not yet experienced military campaigns, the responsibility for the three armies was entirely entrusted to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiaogong had little field experience, Gaozu entrusted the entire army to Jing.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，集兵於夔州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he assembled troops at Qie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That August he gathered his forces at Qie Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 銑以時屬秋潦，江水泛漲，三峽路險，必謂靖不能進，遂休兵不設備。

translations.literal: Xian, because the season was autumn floods, the Yangzi waters were swollen and overflowing, and the Three Gorges route was perilous, was certain Jing could not advance, and therefore rested his troops and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian reckoned that autumn floods had swollen the Yangzi, that the Three Gorges were impassable, and that Jing could not advance — so he stood his army down and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 九月，靖乃率師而進，將下峽，諸將皆請停兵以待水退，靖曰：「兵貴神速，機不可失。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jing then led his army forward; about to descend the gorges, all the generals asked to halt the army and wait for the waters to recede; Jing said, "In warfare speed is prized; opportunity must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jing led his army forward. As they were about to enter the gorges, every general urged a halt until the floods subsided. Jing said, "War prizes speed — the moment must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 今兵始集，銑尚未知，若乘水漲之勢，倏忽至城下，所謂疾雷不及掩耳，此兵家上策。

translations.literal: Now the army has only just assembled and Xian does not yet know; if we ride the momentum of the rising waters and in an instant reach beneath his walls, this is what is called thunder so swift one cannot cover one's ears — this is the supreme stratagem of the military art.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces have only just gathered and Xian does not yet know it. If we ride the flood and reach his walls in a flash, it will be like thunder before he can cover his ears — the supreme stratagem of war.

sentences.zh: 縱彼知我，倉卒徵兵，無以應敵，此必成擒也。

translations.literal: Even if he learns of us, if he hastily levies troops he will have no means to meet the enemy — this will surely end in capture.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he learns of us, he cannot levy troops in time to meet us — we are sure to take him.

sentences.zh: 」孝恭從之，進兵至夷陵。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong followed him and advanced the army to Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong agreed and pushed on to Yiling.

sentences.zh: 銑將文士弘率精兵數萬屯清江，孝恭欲擊之，靖曰：「士弘，銑之健將，士卒驍勇，今新失荊門，盡兵出戰，此是救敗之師，恐不可當也。

translations.literal: Xian's general Wen Shihong led tens of thousands of elite troops encamped at Qingjiang; Xiaogong wished to attack him; Jing said, "Shihong is Xian's stalwart general and his soldiers are fierce and brave; now having newly lost Jingmen, he has committed all his troops to battle — this is an army rescuing defeat and I fear it cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian's general Wen Shihong had tens of thousands of crack troops at Qingjiang. Xiaogong wanted to attack at once. Jing said, "Shihong is Xian's best commander and his men fight fiercely. Having just lost Jingmen, he has thrown his whole force into the field — an army fighting to reverse defeat. I fear we cannot face them head-on.

sentences.zh: 宜自泊南岸，勿與爭鋒，待其氣衰，然後奮擊，破之必矣。

translations.literal: It is fitting to moor on the south bank ourselves and not contend for the edge; wait until their spirit declines, then strike with full force — breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: We should anchor on the south bank and refuse battle until their ardor fades, then strike hard — and we are sure to break them.

sentences.zh: 」孝恭不從，留靖守營，率師與賊合戰。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong did not follow him, left Jing to guard the camp, and led the army to join battle with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong would not listen. He left Jing to hold the camp and led his army into battle.

sentences.zh: 孝恭果敗，奔於南岸。

translations.literal: Xiaogong was indeed defeated and fled to the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong was indeed beaten and fled to the south bank.

sentences.zh: 賊舟大掠，人皆負重。

translations.literal: The enemy boats plundered heavily and every man was laden with booty.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy ships looted freely and every man was weighed down with plunder.

sentences.zh: 靖見其軍亂，縱兵擊破之，獲其舟艦四百餘艘，斬首及溺死將萬人。

translations.literal: Jing saw their army in disorder and unleashed his troops to break them, capturing more than four hundred of their boats, and those beheaded and drowned in the river approached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing their ranks in disorder, Jing loosed his troops and routed them, taking more than four hundred vessels and killing nearly ten thousand by blade and drowning.

sentences.zh: 孝恭遣靖率輕兵五千為先鋒，至江陵，屯營於城下。

translations.literal: Xiaogong dispatched Jing to lead five thousand light troops as vanguard; reaching Jiangling, he encamped beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong sent Jing ahead with five thousand light troops. Reaching Jiangling, he pitched camp below the walls.

sentences.zh: 士弘既敗，銑甚懼，始徵兵於江南，果不能至。

translations.literal: After Shihong was defeated, Xian was greatly afraid and only then began levying troops south of the Yangzi, but in truth they could not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: With Shihong defeated, Xian was terrified and only then began raising troops south of the river — but they never arrived.

sentences.zh: 孝恭以大軍繼進，靖又破其驍將楊君茂、鄭文秀，俘甲卒四千餘人，更勒兵圍銑城。

translations.literal: Xiaogong followed with the main army; Jing again defeated his fierce generals Yang Junmao and Zheng Wenxiu, captured more than four thousand armored soldiers, and again drove the army to besiege Xian's city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong came up with the main force. Jing defeated Xian's crack generals Yang Junmao and Zheng Wenxiu, took more than four thousand armored men prisoner, and pressed the siege of Xian's city.

sentences.zh: 明日，銑遣使請降，靖即入據其城，號令嚴肅，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: The next day Xian sent envoys to request surrender; Jing immediately entered and occupied his city; his orders were strict and solemn, and the army took nothing for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xian sent envoys to surrender. Jing entered the city at once, enforced strict discipline, and allowed no private looting.

sentences.zh: 時諸將咸請孝恭云：「銑之將帥與官軍拒戰死者，罪狀既重，請籍沒其家，以賞將士。

translations.literal: At that time all the generals alike asked Xiaogong, saying, "Xian's commanders and officers who died resisting the imperial army — their crimes are already grave; we ask to register and confiscate their households to reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all urged Xiaogong: "Xian's officers who died fighting us are guilty of grave crimes — let us confiscate their households to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 」靖曰：「王者之師，義存吊伐。

translations.literal: " Jing said, "The army of a true king keeps righteousness in succoring the afflicted and punishing the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing said, "The army of a true king exists to succor the suffering and punish the guilty.

sentences.zh: 百姓既受驅逼，拒戰豈其所願？

translations.literal: The common people, having been driven and compelled, resisted in battle — how could that be their own wish?
translations.idiomatic: The people were driven to fight — how could resistance have been their wish?

sentences.zh: 且犬吠非其主，無容同叛逆之科，此蒯通所以免大戮於漢祖也。

translations.literal: Moreover, a dog barks not at its own master — one cannot lump them together under the category of rebellion; this is why Kuai Tong escaped great execution at the hands of the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a dog barks at a stranger, not its master — they cannot be classed with rebels. That is why Kuai Tong escaped execution under the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 今新定荊、郢，宜弘寬大，以慰遠近之心，降而籍之，恐非救焚拯溺之義。

translations.literal: Now that Jing and Ying are newly pacified, it is fitting to extend magnanimity to comfort hearts near and far; to register and confiscate those who have surrendered — I fear this is not the meaning of rescuing from fire and saving from drowning.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Ying are newly pacified — we should show magnanimity to reassure hearts near and far. To confiscate the property of men who have surrendered is hardly the spirit of rescuing those in fire and flood.

sentences.zh: 但恐自此已南城鎮，各堅守不下，非計之善。

translations.literal: I only fear that from this point the southern walled towns and garrisons will each hold firm and refuse to submit — that would not be a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that from this day every southern town will hold out stubbornly — that would be poor policy.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 江、漢之域，聞之莫不爭下。

translations.literal: Throughout the lands of the Jiang and Han, on hearing of it none failed to vie to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Jiang and Han regions, every district rushed to submit on hearing of it.

sentences.zh: 以功授上柱國，封永康縣公，賜物二千五百段。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Pillar of the State and enfeoffed as Duke of Yongkang County, with a gift of two thousand five hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Yongkang County, and given two thousand five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 詔命檢校荊州刺史，承制拜授。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to act as Inspector of Jing Prefecture and to appoint and invest by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as acting Inspector of Jing Prefecture with authority to appoint and invest officials on the emperor's behalf.

sentences.zh: 乃度嶺至桂州，遣人分道招撫，其大首領馮盎、李光度、寧真長等皆遣子弟來謁，靖承製授其官爵。

translations.literal: He then crossed the ranges to Gui Prefecture, sent men by separate routes to win over and pacify, and the great chieftains Feng Ang, Li Guangdu, Ning Zhenchang, and others all sent sons and younger brothers to pay court; Jing, by imperial commission, granted them offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the ranges into Gui Prefecture and sent parties by several routes to win over the tribes. The great chieftains Feng Ang, Li Guangdu, Ning Zhenchang, and others all sent sons or younger brothers to pay court, and Jing invested them with offices and titles by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 凡所懷輯九十六州，戶六十餘萬。

translations.literal: In all, those he brought to allegiance numbered ninety-six prefectures and more than six hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In all he brought ninety-six prefectures and more than six hundred thousand households into allegiance.

sentences.zh: 優詔勞勉，授嶺南道撫慰大使，檢校桂州總管。

translations.literal: A gracious edict commended and encouraged him; he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Lingnan Circuit and acting Commander of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of praise and encouragement appointed him Pacification Commissioner for the Lingnan circuit and acting commander of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十六年，輔公祏於丹陽反，詔孝恭為元帥、靖為副以討之，李勣、任瑰、張鎮州、黃君漢等七總管並受節度。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Fu Gongshi rebelled at Danyang; an edict made Xiaogong supreme commander and Jing his deputy to suppress him; Li Ji, Ren Gui, Zhang Zhenzhou, Huang Junhan, and seven commanders in all were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Fu Gongshi rebelled at Danyang. Xiaogong was named supreme commander with Jing as his deputy to suppress him. Li Ji, Ren Gui, Zhang Zhenzhou, Huang Junhan, and six other commanders were all placed under their command.

sentences.zh: 師次舒州，公礻石遣將馮惠亮率舟師三萬屯當涂，陳正通、徐紹宗領步騎二萬屯青林山，仍於梁山連鐵鎖以斷江路，築卻月城，延袤十餘里，與惠亮為犄角之勢。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Shu Prefecture, Gongshi dispatched his general Feng Huiliang to lead thirty thousand river troops encamped at Dangtu; Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong led twenty thousand foot and horse encamped at Qinglin Mountain; moreover at Liang Mountain they linked iron chains to cut the river route, built the Receding Moon Fortress extending more than ten li, and formed a pincer position with Huiliang.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Shu Prefecture. Gongshi sent Feng Huiliang with thirty thousand river troops to hold Dangtu, while Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong held Qinglin Mountain with twenty thousand foot and horse. At Liang Mountain they stretched iron chains across the river, built the Receding Moon fortress for more than ten li, and formed a pincer with Huiliang's fleet.

sentences.zh: 孝恭集諸將會議，皆云：「惠亮、正通並握強兵，為不戰之計，城柵既固，卒不可攻。

translations.literal: Xiaogong gathered the generals for council; all said, "Huiliang and Zhengtong both hold strong armies and plan not to give battle; their walls and palisades are already solid and in the end cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong called a council of his generals. All said, "Huiliang and Zhengtong hold strong forces and mean to avoid battle. Their fortifications are too solid to storm.

sentences.zh: 請直指丹陽，掩其巢穴，丹陽既破，惠亮自降。

translations.literal: We ask to strike directly at Danyang and seize their nest; once Danyang is broken, Huiliang will surrender of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Let us march straight on Danyang and strike their nest. Once Danyang falls, Huiliang will surrender of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 」孝恭欲從其議。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong wished to follow their proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong was inclined to agree.

sentences.zh: 靖曰：「公祏精銳，雖在水陸二軍，然其自統之兵，亦皆勁勇。

translations.literal: Jing said, "Gongshi's elite troops, though divided between river and land armies, yet the troops he commands in person are also all stalwart and brave.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Gongshi's best troops may be split between river and land, but the men he leads himself are all crack fighters.

sentences.zh: 惠亮等城柵尚不可攻，公祏既保石頭，豈應易拔？

translations.literal: Huiliang's walls and palisades still cannot be attacked — if Gongshi already holds Stone City, how should it be easy to pull up?
translations.idiomatic: If Huiliang's fortifications cannot be taken, how can we expect to pluck Gongshi easily from Stone City?

sentences.zh: 若我師至丹陽，留停旬月，進則公祏未平，退則惠亮為患，此便腹背受敵，恐非萬全之計。

translations.literal: If our army reaches Danyang and lingers half a month, advancing yet Gongshi is not pacified, retreating yet Huiliang becomes a threat — this would be attacked front and rear; I fear it is not a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: If we reach Danyang and linger half a month, Gongshi will still stand before us while Huiliang threatens our rear — we would be caught between two fires. That is no sure plan.

sentences.zh: 惠亮、正通皆是百戰餘賊，必不憚於野戰，止為公祏立計，令其持重，但欲不戰，以老我師。

translations.literal: Huiliang and Zhengtong are both battle-hardened remnants of rebels and surely do not fear field combat; they act only to set plans for Gongshi, making him hold his weight, wishing only not to fight in order to wear out our army.
translations.idiomatic: Huiliang and Zhengtong are hardened veterans and are not afraid of field battle. They act only for Gongshi's sake, counseling him to stand on the defensive and wear our army down without fighting.

sentences.zh: 今欲攻其城柵，乃是出其不意，滅賊之機，唯在此舉。

translations.literal: Now if we wish to attack their walls and palisades, this is to catch them unawares — the opportunity to destroy the rebels lies solely in this move.
translations.idiomatic: To strike their fortifications now is to catch them unawares — our chance to destroy the rebels lies in this move alone.

sentences.zh: 」孝恭然之。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong agreed.

sentences.zh: 靖乃率黃君漢等先擊惠亮，苦戰破之，殺傷乃溺死者萬餘人，惠亮奔走。

translations.literal: Jing then led Huang Junhan and others to strike Huiliang first; after bitter fighting he broke him; those killed, wounded, and drowned totaled more than ten thousand; Huiliang fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing led Huang Junhan and others against Huiliang first. After a hard fight he broke the enemy fleet, killing or drowning more than ten thousand men, and Huiliang fled.

sentences.zh: 靖率輕兵先至丹陽，公祏大懼。

translations.literal: Jing led light troops to reach Danyang first; Gongshi was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jing pressed ahead with light troops to Danyang, and Gongshi was terrified.

sentences.zh: 先遣偽將左遊仙領兵守會稽以為引援，公祏擁兵東走，以趨遊仙，至吳郡，與惠亮、正通並相次擒獲，江南悉平。

translations.literal: He first dispatched the false general Zuo Youxian to lead troops guarding Kuaiji as reinforcement; Gongshi gathered his army and fled east to join Youxian; reaching Wu Commandery, he and Huiliang and Zhengtong were captured one after another, and the entire south of the Yangzi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the rebel general Zuo Youxian to hold Kuaiji as a reserve and fled east with his army to join him. At Wu Commandery he was captured, followed in turn by Huiliang and Zhengtong, and the entire south was pacified.

sentences.zh: 於是置東南道行台，拜靖行台兵部尚書，賜物千段、奴婢百口、馬百匹。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Southeast Circuit Executive was established; Jing was appointed Executive Minister of War and given a thousand bolts of goods, a hundred slave women, and a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Southeast Circuit Executive was then established, and Jing was made its Minister of War, with gifts of a thousand bolts of silk, a hundred slave women, and a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 其年，行台廢，又檢校揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: That year the Executive was abolished, and he was again made acting Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Area.
translations.idiomatic: That year the executive was abolished, and he was made acting chief administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan command.

sentences.zh: 丹陽連罹兵寇，百姓凋弊，靖鎮撫之，吳、楚以安。

translations.literal: Danyang had suffered repeated military raids and the common people were depleted; Jing pacified and comforted them, and Wu and Chu were thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang had suffered repeated warfare and the people were destitute. Jing pacified the region, and Wu and Chu were restored to calm.

sentences.zh: 八年，突厥寇太原，以靖為行軍總管，統江淮兵一萬，與張瑾屯大谷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Turks raided Taiyuan; Jing was made Campaign Commander, commanding ten thousand troops from the Jiang and Huai, and with Zhang Jin encamped at Dagu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the Turks raided Taiyuan. Jing was made campaign commander of ten thousand troops from the Jiang and Huai regions and, with Zhang Jin, encamped at Dagu Valley.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍不利，靖眾獨全。

translations.literal: At that time the various armies fared poorly, but Jing's force alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: While other armies fared badly, Jing's force alone came through unscathed.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校安州大都督。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made acting Metropolitan Commander of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting metropolitan commander of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖每云：「李靖是蕭銑、輔公祏膏肓，古之名將韓、白、衛、霍，豈能及也！

translations.literal: Gaozu often said, "Li Jing is the vital organ disease of Xiao Xian and Fu Gongshi — could the famous generals of old, Han, Bai, Wei, and Huo, compare with him!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often said, "Li Jing was the mortal sickness of Xiao Xian and Fu Gongshi — how could the great captains of old, Han Xin, Bai Qi, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing, match him?

sentences.zh: 」九年，突厥莫賀咄設寇邊，征靖為靈州道行軍總管。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year the Turkic Mohezhuo she raided the frontier; Jing was summoned as Campaign Commander of the Lingzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " In year 9 the Turkic khan Mohezhuo raided the frontier, and Jing was summoned as campaign commander on the Lingzhou route.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗入涇陽，靖率兵倍道趨豳州，邀賊歸路，既而與虜和親而罷。

translations.literal: Khan Jieli entered Jingyang; Jing led his army by forced marches toward Bin Prefecture to intercept the enemy's line of retreat; afterward peace through marriage alliance with the barbarians was concluded and the campaign ended.
translations.idiomatic: When Khan Jieli reached Jingyang, Jing forced his march to Bin Prefecture to cut the Turks' retreat. Soon afterward a marriage alliance was concluded with the nomads and the campaign ended.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，拜刑部尚書，並錄前後功，賜實封四百戶。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Jing was appointed Minister of Punishments, and his former and later achievements were all recorded, with a grant of four hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Jing was appointed Minister of Punishments. His past and present achievements were recorded together, and he received a substantive fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，以本官兼檢校中書令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, with his existing office he was concurrently made acting Central Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 2 he was made acting Director of the Central Secretariat while retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was transferred to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 突厥諸部離叛，朝廷將圖進取，以靖為代州道行軍總管，率驍騎三千，自馬邑出其不意，直趨惡陽嶺以逼之。

translations.literal: The various Turkic tribes split away in rebellion; the court planned an advance to seize them; Jing was made Campaign Commander of the Daizhou Circuit, leading three thousand elite cavalry from Mayi by surprise, pressing straight to Wuyang Ridge to corner them.
translations.idiomatic: As the Turkic tribes broke away, the court prepared an offensive and made Jing campaign commander on the Daizhou route. He led three thousand elite horsemen from Mayi in a surprise march straight to Wuyang Ridge to press the enemy.

sentences.zh: 突利可汗不虞於靖，見官軍奄至，於是大懼，相謂曰：「唐兵若不傾國而來，靖豈敢孤軍而至？

translations.literal: Khan Tuli did not anticipate Jing; seeing the imperial army arrive suddenly, he was greatly afraid and said to one another, "If Tang troops had not come with the full strength of the state, how would Jing dare come with a lone army?
translations.idiomatic: Khan Tuli had not expected Jing. When the imperial army appeared without warning, he was terrified and his men said to one another, "If the Tang had not sent their full strength, how would Jing dare come alone?

sentences.zh: 」一日數驚。

translations.literal: " Several times in a single day they were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: " They were alarmed several times in a single day.

sentences.zh: 靖候知之，潛令間諜離其心腹，其所親康蘇密來降。

translations.literal: Jing observed and knew this; he secretly ordered spies to sunder their inner circle, and Tuli's close associate Kang Sumi came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jing saw his chance and secretly sent agents to sow discord among the khan's inner circle. Tuli's close associate Kang Sumi came over to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 四年，靖進擊定襄，破之，獲隋齊王暕之子楊正道及煬帝蕭后，送於京師，可汗僅以身遁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jing advanced to attack Dingxiang and broke it, capturing the Sui Prince of Qi Yang Zhengdao, son of Yang Guang, and Empress Xiao of Emperor Yang, and sending them to the capital; the khan escaped only with his own person.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Jing advanced against Dingxiang and took it, capturing the Sui prince Yang Zhengdao, son of Prince of Qi Yang Zhao, and Empress Xiao of Emperor Yang, whom he sent to the capital. The khan escaped with only his own person.

sentences.zh: 以功進封代國公，賜物六百段及名馬、寶器焉。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Duke of the State of Dai, with gifts of six hundred bolts of goods and famous horses and precious vessels.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was advanced to Duke of Dai, with six hundred bolts of silk, fine horses, and precious vessels.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂曰：「昔李陵提步卒五千，不免身降匈奴，尚得書名竹帛。

translations.literal: Taizong once said to him, "In former times Li Ling led five thousand foot soldiers yet could not avoid surrendering in person to the Xiongnu, and still won his name written on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once told him, "Long ago Li Ling led five thousand foot soldiers yet still fell captive to the Xiongnu — and his name was written into history nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 卿以三千輕騎深入虜庭，克復定襄，威振北狄，古今所未有，足報往年渭水之役。

translations.literal: You with three thousand light cavalry penetrated deep into the barbarian court, recovered Dingxiang, and shook the northern Di — nothing like it in past or present — enough to repay the battle at the Wei River in former years.
translations.idiomatic: You took three thousand light horsemen deep into the steppe, recovered Dingxiang, and shook the northern tribes — a feat unmatched in any age, and enough to answer for the battle at the Wei River years ago.

sentences.zh: 」自破定襄後，頡利可汗大懼，退保鐵山，遣使入朝謝罪，請舉國內附。

translations.literal: " After Dingxiang was broken, Khan Jieli was greatly afraid, withdrew to hold Iron Mountain, sent envoys to court to confess guilt, and requested to submit the entire nation.
translations.idiomatic: " After the fall of Dingxiang, Khan Jieli was terrified. He withdrew to Iron Mountain, sent envoys to court to confess his crimes, and asked to submit his whole people.

sentences.zh: 又以靖為定襄道行軍總管，往迎頡利。

translations.literal: Jing was again made Campaign Commander of the Dingxiang Circuit to go welcome Jieli.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was again made campaign commander on the Dingxiang route and sent to receive Jieli.

sentences.zh: 頡利雖外請朝謁，而潛懷猶豫。

translations.literal: Although Jieli outwardly requested an audience at court, inwardly he secretly harbored hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jieli asked to come to court, he still hesitated in secret.

sentences.zh: 其年二月，太宗遣鴻臚卿唐儉、將軍安修仁慰諭，靖揣知其意，謂將軍張公謹曰：「詔使到彼，虜必自寬。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year Taizong dispatched Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Jian and General An Xiuren to comfort and instruct him; Jing divined his intent and said to General Zhang Gongjin, "When the imperial envoys reach them, the barbarians will surely relax on their own.
translations.idiomatic: That February Taizong sent the Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Jian and General An Xiuren to reassure him. Jing read his mind and told General Zhang Gongjin, "When the envoys arrive, the Turks will surely let down their guard.

sentences.zh: 遂選精騎一萬，齎二十日糧，引兵自白道襲之。

translations.literal: He then selected ten thousand elite cavalry, carried twenty days' provisions, and led the army by the White Route to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He chose ten thousand elite horsemen, loaded twenty days' rations, and led them down the White Route in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 」公謹曰：「詔許其降，行人在彼，未宜討擊。

translations.literal: " Gongjin said, "The edict has permitted their surrender; the envoys are there—it is not yet appropriate to mount an attack.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Gongjin said, "The throne has already accepted their surrender, and our envoys are among them. It is not yet the time to strike."

sentences.zh: 」靖曰：「此兵機也，時不可失，韓信所以破齊也。

translations.literal: " Jing said, "This is a military opportunity; the moment must not be lost—this is how Han Xin broke Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing replied, "This is the chance war gives us, and the moment will not wait. It is how Han Xin destroyed Qi."

sentences.zh: 如唐儉等輩，何足可惜。

translations.literal: Men like Tang Jian and the rest—what is there to regret losing?
translations.idiomatic: As for men like Tang Jian, they are hardly worth grieving over.

sentences.zh: 」督軍疾進，師至陰山，遇其斥候千餘帳，皆俘以隨軍。

translations.literal: " He urged the army forward at speed; when the force reached Yinshan, it encountered more than a thousand of their scout encampments and took them all captive to accompany the army.
translations.idiomatic: " He drove the army forward at full speed. When they reached Yinshan they overran more than a thousand Turk scout camps and took every man captive to march with the column.

sentences.zh: 頡利見使者，大悅，不虞官兵至也。

translations.literal: Jieli received the envoys and was greatly pleased, never suspecting that government troops would arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli welcomed the envoys in high spirits, never imagining that imperial troops were already near.

sentences.zh: 靖軍將逼其牙帳十五里，虜始覺。

translations.literal: When Jing's army was about to press within fifteen li of his royal encampment, the barbarians only then became aware.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Jing's army was within fifteen li of the khan's camp did the Turks realize what was happening.

sentences.zh: 頡利畏威先走，部眾因而潰散。

translations.literal: Jieli, in fear of their might, fled first, and his followers thereupon broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli fled ahead of the rest, terrified by their strength, and his host collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 靖斬萬餘級，俘男女十餘萬，殺其妻隋義成公主。

translations.literal: Jing beheaded more than ten thousand and took captive men and women numbering over a hundred thousand; he killed Jieli's wife, the Sui Princess Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's men took more than ten thousand heads and over a hundred thousand captives, and killed Jieli's wife, the Sui princess Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 頡利乘千里馬將走投吐谷渾，西道行軍總管張寶相擒之以獻。

translations.literal: Jieli mounted a thousand-li horse and was about to flee toward Tuyuhun when Zhang Baoxiang, campaign commander of the Western Route, captured him and presented him as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli fled on a swift horse toward Tuyuhun, but Zhang Baoxiang, commander on the western route, captured him and sent him in.

sentences.zh: 俄而突利可汗來奔，遂復定襄、常安之地，斥土界自陰山北至於大漠。

translations.literal: Before long Khan Tuli came to surrender; the lands of Dingxiang and Chang'an were thus recovered, and the frontier was extended from Yinshan northward to the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Khan Tuli came over to the Tang side. Dingxiang and Chang'an were restored, and the border was pushed from Yinshan north to the edge of the desert.

sentences.zh: 太宗初聞靖破頡利，大悅，謂侍臣曰：「朕聞主憂臣辱，主辱臣死。

translations.literal: When Taizong first heard that Jing had broken Jieli, he was greatly pleased and said to his attending ministers, "I have heard that when the lord grieves, the minister is shamed; when the lord is shamed, the minister dies.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong first heard that Jing had broken Jieli, he was overjoyed and told his ministers, "They say that when the ruler is troubled, the minister feels shame, and when the ruler is shamed, the minister should die."

sentences.zh: 往者國家草創，太上皇以百姓之故，稱臣於突厥，朕未嘗不痛心疾首，志滅匈奴，坐不安席，食不甘味。

translations.literal: In former days, when the state was newly founded, the Retired Emperor, for the sake of the people, called himself subject to the Turks; I have never failed to feel heart-piercing grief, resolved to destroy the Xiongnu, unable to sit at ease or find flavor in food.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was first being built, the Retired Emperor bowed to the Turks for the people's sake. I have never ceased to burn with shame and rage, longing to destroy them, unable to rest in my seat or taste my food.

sentences.zh: 今者暫動偏師，無往不捷，單于款塞，恥其雪乎！

translations.literal: Now, with a partial force briefly deployed, nowhere have we not been victorious; the chanyu has come in submission to the border—is not the shame washed away!
translations.idiomatic: Now a single wing of the army has moved out and won everywhere it went. The chanyu has come to the frontier in submission—has that shame not been wiped clean!

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦天下，酺五日。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm and ordered five days of public feasting.
translations.idiomatic: " He then granted a general amnesty to the empire and declared five days of celebration.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫溫彥博害其功，譖靖軍無綱紀，致令虜中奇寶，散於亂兵之手。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wen Yanbo, envious of his achievement, slandered Jing, saying his army lacked discipline and had allowed rare treasures among the barbarians to be scattered into the hands of disorderly soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wen Yanbo, jealous of Jing's victory, accused him of letting his troops run wild so that the Turks' rare treasures fell into the hands of looting soldiers.

sentences.zh: 太宗大加責讓，靖頓首謝。

translations.literal: Taizong rebuked him severely, and Jing kowtowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sharply reproached him, and Jing prostrated himself in apology.

sentences.zh: 久之，太宗謂曰：「隋將史萬歲破達頭可汗，有功不賞，以罪致戮。

translations.literal: After some time, Taizong said to him, "The Sui general Shi Wansui broke Khan Datou, yet received no reward for his merit and was put to death on a charge.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Taizong told him, "Under the Sui, the general Shi Wansui defeated Khan Datou, but his merit went unrewarded and he was executed on a false charge."

sentences.zh: 朕則不然，當赦公之罪，錄公之勳。

translations.literal: I am not like that; I shall pardon your offense and record your merit.
translations.idiomatic: I am not like that. I will pardon your faults and honor your achievements.

sentences.zh: 」詔加左光祿大夫，賜絹千匹，真食邑通前五百戶。

translations.literal: " An edict promoted him to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, granted a thousand bolts of silk, and made his fief households permanently five hundred in all with previous holdings.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict appointed him Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, gave him a thousand bolts of silk, and confirmed his permanent fief at five hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太宗謂靖曰：「前有人讒公，今朕意已悟，公勿以為懷。

translations.literal: Before long, Taizong said to Jing, "Before this someone slandered you; now my mind is clear, and you should not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Taizong told Jing, "Someone slandered you before, but I see clearly now. Do not let it weigh on you."

sentences.zh: 」賜絹二千匹，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: " He granted two thousand bolts of silk and appointed him Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him two thousand bolts of silk and made him Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 靖性沉厚，每與時宰參議，恂恂然似不能言。

translations.literal: Jing's nature was deep and steady; whenever he joined the chief ministers in deliberation, he was deferential, as though unable to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was grave and reserved by nature. In council with the chief ministers he was so deferential that he seemed barely able to speak at all.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔為畿內道大使，伺察風俗。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to serve as envoy of the Metropolitan Circuit to inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed envoy of the metropolitan circuit to inspect local customs.

sentences.zh: 尋以足疾上表乞骸骨，言甚懇至。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on account of illness in his feet, he submitted a memorial requesting to retire his bones; his words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he petitioned to retire on account of a foot ailment, in language of deep sincerity.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣中書侍郎岑文本謂曰：「朕觀自古已來，身居富貴，能知止足者甚少。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben to say to him, "I observe that from ancient times until now, among those dwelling in wealth and honor, very few have known when to stop and be satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent the Vice Director of the Secretariat, Cen Wenben, to tell him, "From ancient times until now, I have seen few men who stood in wealth and power and knew when they had enough."

sentences.zh: 不問愚智，莫能自知，才雖不堪，強欲居職，縱有疾病，猶自勉強。

translations.literal: Whether foolish or wise, none can know themselves; though their talent cannot bear the burden, they forcibly wish to hold office, and even if they have illness, they still force themselves on.
translations.idiomatic: Wise or foolish, almost none can judge themselves honestly. Even when unfit for office they cling to rank, and even when ill they drag themselves back to duty.

sentences.zh: 公能識達大體，深足可嘉，朕今非直成公雅志，欲以公為一代楷模。

translations.literal: You can discern and grasp the larger pattern—it is deeply worthy of praise; I now am not merely fulfilling your lofty wish, but wish to make you a model for an entire generation.
translations.idiomatic: You understand the larger truth, and that is deeply admirable. I am not only granting your wish; I mean to hold you up as a model for your whole generation.

sentences.zh: 」乃下優詔，加授特進，聽在第攝養。

translations.literal: " He then issued a gracious edict, additionally appointing him Special Advance, and permitted him to recuperate at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: " He then issued a gracious edict, promoted him to Special Advance, and allowed him to convalesce at home.

sentences.zh: 賜物千段、尚乘馬兩匹，祿賜、國官府佐，並依舊給，患若小瘳，每三兩日至門下、中書平章政事。

translations.literal: He granted a thousand lengths of goods and two imperial stable horses; salary, gifts, and household and office attendants were all supplied as before; if the illness should ease somewhat, he was to attend every two or three days at the Secretariat and Chancellery to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him a thousand lengths of goods and two horses from the imperial stables. Salary, perquisites, and household staff were unchanged. If his illness eased, he was to attend deliberations at the Secretariat and Chancellery every few days.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，賜靖靈壽杖，助足疾也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he granted Jing a lingzhi cane to assist with his foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he gave Jing a cane of lingzhi wood to help him with his foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吐谷渾寇邊，太宗顧謂侍臣曰：「得李靖為帥，豈非善也！

translations.literal: Before long, when Tuyuhun raided the frontier, Taizong turned and said to his attending ministers, "To have Li Jing as commander—would that not be excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tuyuhun raided the border. Taizong turned to his ministers and said, "If only we could have Li Jing as commander—would that not be ideal!"

sentences.zh: 」靖乃見房玄齡曰：「靖雖年老，固堪一行。

translations.literal: " Jing thereupon went to see Fang Xuanling and said, "Though Jing is old in years, he is indeed fit for one campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing went to Fang Xuanling and said, "I am old, but I am still equal to one more campaign."

sentences.zh: 」太宗大悅，即以靖為西海道行軍大總管，統兵部尚書、任城王道宗、涼州都督李大亮、右衛將軍李道彥、利州刺史高甑生等三總管征之。

translations.literal: " Taizong was greatly pleased and immediately made Jing Grand Campaign Commander of the Western Sea Route, commanding Minister of War Prince Daozong of Rencheng, Liangzhou Area Commander Li Daliang, General of the Right Guard Li Daoyan, Governor of Li Prefecture Gao Zengsheng, and the other three route commanders to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong was delighted and at once made Jing grand campaign commander on the Western Sea route, putting him over Minister of War Prince Daozong of Rencheng, Liangzhou commander Li Daliang, General of the Right Guard Li Daoyan, Li Prefecture governor Gao Zengsheng, and the other route commanders for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 九年，軍次伏俟城，吐谷渾燒去野草，以餧我師，退保大非川，諸將咸言春草未生，馬已羸瘦，不可赴敵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the army halted at Fuqi City; Tuyuhun burned away the wild grasses to starve our army and withdrew to hold Da Feichuan. All the generals said that spring grass had not yet grown and the horses were already emaciated, so they could not go to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: That year the army reached Fuqi City. Tuyuhun burned the pasture to starve the Tang horses and fell back on Da Feichuan. The generals all said the spring grass had not yet come in, the horses were already thin, and they could not advance to fight.

sentences.zh: 唯靖決計而進，深入敵境，遂逾積石山。

translations.literal: Only Jing resolved on a plan and advanced, penetrating deep into enemy territory and crossing over Jishi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Jing alone decided to press on. He drove deep into enemy country and crossed Jishi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 前後戰數十合，殺傷甚眾，大破其國。

translations.literal: In battles before and after, numbering several tens of engagements, casualties were very numerous, and their state was greatly broken.
translations.idiomatic: In dozens of engagements they killed and wounded vast numbers of the enemy and broke Tuyuhun's power.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾之眾遂殺其可汗來降，靖又立大寧王慕容順而還。

translations.literal: The people of Tuyuhun thereupon killed their khan and came to surrender; Jing also installed Prince Ning of Dading, Murong Shun, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun then killed their own khan and submitted. Jing installed Prince Ning of Dading, Murong Shun, as ruler and marched home.

sentences.zh: 初，利州刺史高甑生為鹽澤道總管，以後軍期，靖薄責之，甑生因有憾於靖。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Governor of Li Prefecture Gao Zengsheng served as route commander of the Salt Marsh Route, he arrived late and missed the rendezvous; Jing lightly rebuked him, and Zengsheng therefore bore resentment toward Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Li Prefecture governor Gao Zengsheng served as commander on the Salt Marsh route, he had arrived late. Jing rebuked him lightly, and from that Zengsheng nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及是，與廣州都督府長史唐奉義告靖謀反。

translations.literal: At this time, together with Chief Clerk of the Guangzhou Area Command Tang Fengyi, he reported that Jing was plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Now he joined with Tang Fengyi, chief clerk of the Guangzhou area command, in accusing Jing of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 太宗命法官按其事，甑生等竟以誣罔得罪。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered judicial officials to investigate the matter, and Zengsheng and the others were in the end found guilty of false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered a judicial inquiry, and Zengsheng and his accomplices were convicted of slander.

sentences.zh: 靖乃闔門自守，杜絕賓客，雖親戚不得妄進。

translations.literal: Jing thereupon shut his gates and kept himself within, cutting off all guests; even relatives were not permitted to enter without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then shut his gates and withdrew from the world. He refused all visitors, and even kinsmen were not allowed in without good reason.

sentences.zh: 十一年，改封衛國公，授濮州刺史，仍令代襲，例竟不行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, appointed Governor of Pu Prefecture, and again ordered that the title pass in succession; the precedent was ultimately not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was re-created Duke of Wei and made governor of Pu Prefecture. Hereditary succession was again ordered, but the practice was never actually applied.

sentences.zh: 十四年，靖妻卒，有詔墳塋制度，依漢衛、霍故事；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Jing's wife died; an edict ordered the tomb and burial arrangements to follow the Han precedents of Wei and Huo;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Jing's wife died. An edict ordered that her tomb be laid out after the Han precedents of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing;

sentences.zh: 築闕象突厥內鐵山、吐谷渾內積石山形，以旌殊績。

translations.literal: a memorial gate was built shaped like Iron Mountain within the Turks and Jishi Mountain within Tuyuhun, to mark his extraordinary achievements.
translations.idiomatic: and a gate-tower was built in the forms of Iron Mountain among the Turks and Jishi Mountain in Tuyuhun, to honor his extraordinary victories.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔圖畫靖及趙郡王孝恭等二十四人於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year an edict ordered portraits painted of Jing and Prince Xiaogong of Zhao Commandery and twenty-four others in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year an edict ordered portraits of Jing, Prince Xiaogong of Zhao Commandery, and twenty-two others painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十八年，帝幸其第問疾，仍賜絹五百匹，進位衛國公、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the emperor visited his residence to inquire after his illness, additionally granted five hundred bolts of silk, and advanced him to Duke of Wei with the honor of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Imperial Regalia of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the emperor visited his home to ask after his health, gave him five hundred bolts of silk, and promoted him to Duke of Wei with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 太宗將伐遼東，召靖入閣，賜坐御前，謂曰：「公南平吳會，北清沙漠，西定慕容，唯東有高麗未服，公意如何？

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to campaign against Liaodong, he summoned Jing into the pavilion, granted him a seat before the throne, and said, "You pacified Wu and Kuaiji in the south, cleared the desert in the north, and settled Murong in the west; only in the east Goguryeo remains unsubmissive—what is your view?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong prepared to campaign against Liaodong, he summoned Jing to the inner hall, seated him before the throne, and said, "You pacified the south, cleared the northern desert, and settled the Murong westward. Only Goguryeo in the east still defies us. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣往者憑藉天威，薄展微效，今殘年朽骨，唯擬此行。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your subject in former days relied on Heaven's majesty and slightly displayed a small effect; now, in my remaining years as withered bones, I intend only this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing answered, "In the past I borrowed the emperor's might and achieved a little. Now, though I am old bones in my last years, this is the campaign I have my heart set on."

sentences.zh: 陛下不棄，老臣病期瘳矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not cast me aside, this old minister's illness may be expected to recover.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not cast me aside, even this old man's illness may yet mend.

sentences.zh: 」太宗愍其羸老，不許。

translations.literal: " Taizong, pitying his frailty and age, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong, moved by pity for his frail age, refused.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，薨於家，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died at home, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he died at home, at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 冊贈司徒、并州都督，給班劍四十人、羽葆鼓吹，陪葬昭陵，謚曰景武。

translations.literal: By patent he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Education and Area Commander of Bingzhou, granted forty ceremonial guards with swords and feathered banners with martial music, buried by accompaniment at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous title Jingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Minister of Education and area commander of Bingzhou, granted forty ceremonial guards and an imperial funeral escort, buried beside Zhaoling, and given the posthumous name Jingwu.

sentences.zh: 子德謇嗣，官至將作少匠。

translations.literal: His son Deqian succeeded him and rose in office to Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deqian succeeded him and rose to vice director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 靖弟客師，貞觀中，官至右武衛將軍，以戰功累封丹陽郡公。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Keshe, in the Zhenguan era, rose in office to General of the Right Martial Guard and was repeatedly enfeoffed for battle achievements as Duke of Danyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Keshe served in the Zhenguan era as general of the Right Martial Guard and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Danyang for his battle honors.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，以年老致仕，性好馳獵，四時從禽，無暫止息。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yonghui era he retired on account of old age; his nature loved riding and hunting, and in all four seasons he followed the chase, never pausing to rest.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yonghui era he retired on account of age. He loved the hunt and rode after game through all four seasons without pause.

sentences.zh: 有別業在昆明池南，自京城之外，西際澧水，鳥獸皆識之，每出則鳥鵲隨逐而噪，野人謂之「鳥賊」。

translations.literal: He had a separate estate south of Kunming Pond; from beyond the capital west to the Li River, birds and beasts all knew him, and whenever he went out birds and magpies would follow in pursuit and cry out; country people called him "the Bird Thief."
translations.idiomatic: He kept a country estate south of Kunming Pond. From beyond the capital west to the Li River, every bird and beast knew him. Whenever he rode out, birds and magpies followed shrieking after him, and country folk called him "the Bird Thief."

sentences.zh: 總章中卒，年九十餘。

translations.literal: He died in the Zongzhang era, aged over ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zongzhang era, aged more than ninety.

sentences.zh: 大和中，令問孫彥芳，鳳翔府司錄參軍，詣闕進高祖、太宗所賜衛國公靖官告、敕書、手詔等十餘卷，內四卷太宗文皇帝筆跡，文宗寶惜不能釋手。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era, Lingwen's descendant Yanfang, Recorder of Fengxiang Prefecture, came to court and presented more than ten scrolls of appointment patents, edicts, and autograph edicts bestowed by Gaozu and Taizong upon Duke of Wei Jing; four scrolls within bore the handwriting of Emperor Wen of Taizong, and Emperor Wenzong treasured them and could not release them from his hands.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dahe era Jing's descendant Yanfang, a recorder in Fengxiang Prefecture, came to court with more than ten scrolls of patents, edicts, and autograph orders that Gaozu and Taizong had given the Duke of Wei. Four bore Taizong's own hand, and Emperor Wenzong treasured them so dearly he could not put them down.

sentences.zh: 其佩筆尚堪書，金裝木匣，製作精巧。

translations.literal: The brush he had worn was still fit for writing; its gold-mounted wooden case was exquisitely made.
translations.idiomatic: Even the brush Jing had carried still wrote well, kept in an exquisitely made case of gold-mounted wood.

sentences.zh: 帝並留禁中，令書工模寫本還之，賜芳絹二百匹、衣服、靴笏以酬之。

translations.literal: The emperor kept them all within the palace precinct, ordered scribes to copy them and return the originals, and granted Yanfang two hundred bolts of silk, clothing, boots, and court tablets as reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept them in the palace, had scribes copy them and returned the originals, and rewarded Yanfang with two hundred bolts of silk, clothing, boots, and court regalia.

sentences.zh: 李勣，曹州離狐人也。

translations.literal: Li Ji was a native of Lihu in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji came from Lihu in Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋末徙居滑州之衛南。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui he moved to Weinan in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui his family moved to Weinan in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本姓徐氏，名世勣，永徽中，以犯太宗諱，單名勣焉。

translations.literal: His original surname was Xu and his name Shiji; in the Yonghui era, because it violated Taizong's taboo name, he took the single name Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Xu and his name Shiji. In the Yonghui era, to avoid Taizong's taboo, he shortened his name to Ji.

sentences.zh: 家多僮僕，積粟數千鐘，與其父蓋皆好惠施，拯濟貧乏，不問親疏。

translations.literal: The household had many servants and retainers and stored grain numbering several thousand zhong; he and his father Gai both loved generous giving, relieving the poor and needy without distinction of kin or stranger.
translations.idiomatic: The household kept many servants and stored several thousand zhong of grain. He and his father Gai were both generous by nature, helping the poor without regard to kin or stranger.

sentences.zh: 大業末，韋城人翟讓聚眾為盜，勣往從之，時年十七，謂讓曰：「今此土地是公及勣鄉壤，人多相識，不宜自相侵掠。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era, Zhai Rang of Weicheng gathered a band and became a robber; Ji went to join him. He was then seventeen and said to Rang, "This land now is the native soil of you and Ji; many people know one another—it is not fitting to plunder one another.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era Zhai Rang of Weicheng raised a band of rebels, and Ji joined him. He was seventeen and told Rang, "This country is yours and mine. The people know one another here. We should not prey on our own neighbors."

sentences.zh: 且宋、鄭兩郡，地管御河，商旅往還，船乘不絕，就彼邀截，足以自相資助。

translations.literal: Moreover, the two commanderies of Song and Zheng lie along the Imperial Canal; merchants and travelers come and go and boats and carts never cease—if we intercept them there, that will suffice for mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Zheng commanderies lie along the Imperial Canal, where merchants and boats pass without end. If we intercept traffic there, we can support ourselves well enough.

sentences.zh: 」讓然之，於是劫公私船取物，兵眾大振。

translations.literal: " Rang agreed; thereupon they plundered public and private boats for goods, and their force greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: " Rang agreed. They began seizing goods from public and private boats, and their force grew rapidly.

sentences.zh: 隋遣齊郡通守張須陀率師二萬討之，勣與頻戰，竟斬須陀於陣。

translations.literal: The Sui dispatched Zhang Xituo, Administrator of Qi Commandery, to lead twenty thousand troops against them; Ji fought him repeatedly and in the end beheaded Xituo in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui sent Zhang Xituo, administrator of Qi Commandery, against them with twenty thousand men. Ji fought him again and again and finally killed him on the field.

sentences.zh: 初，李密亡命在雍丘，浚儀人王伯當匿於野，伯當共勣說翟讓奉密為主。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Mi was a fugitive at Yongqiu; Wang Bodang of Junyi was hiding in the wilds, and Bodang together with Ji persuaded Zhai Rang to take Mi as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Mi was a fugitive at Yongqiu, and Wang Bodang of Junyi was living in hiding. Bodang and Ji together persuaded Zhai Rang to accept Mi as leader.

sentences.zh: 隋令王世充討密，勣以奇計敗世充於洛水之上，密拜勣為東海郡公。

translations.literal: The Sui ordered Wang Shichong to campaign against Mi; Ji with a stratagem defeated Shichong on the Luo River, and Mi enfeoffed Ji as Duke of Donghai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui ordered Wang Shichong to suppress Mi. Ji defeated Shichong on the Luo with a clever stratagem, and Mi created him Duke of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 時河南、山東大水，死者將半，隋帝令飢人就食黎陽，開倉賑給。

translations.literal: At that time Henan and Shandong suffered great floods, and nearly half the people died; the Sui emperor ordered the hungry to go to Liyang for food and opened the granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Shandong were then ravaged by flood, and nearly half the people died. The Sui emperor ordered the hungry to go to Liyang for grain and opened the storehouses for relief.

sentences.zh: 時政教已紊，倉司不時賑給，死者日數萬人。

translations.literal: Government and teaching were already in disorder; the granary officials did not distribute relief in time, and the dead numbered tens of thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: By then government had collapsed into chaos. The granary officials failed to distribute relief in time, and tens of thousands died each day.

sentences.zh: 勣言於密曰：「天下大亂，本是為飢，今若得黎陽一倉，大事濟矣。

translations.literal: Ji said to Mi, "The realm is in great disorder, and at root it is because of hunger; if we can now obtain the one granary at Liyang, the great affair will be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Ji told Mi, "The empire is in chaos because people are starving. If we can take the granary at Liyang, the great enterprise will be won."

sentences.zh: 」密乃遣勣領麾下五千人自原武濟河掩襲，即日克之，開倉恣食，一旬之間，勝兵二十萬餘。

translations.literal: " Mi thereupon dispatched Ji to lead five thousand men under his command to cross the river from Yuanwu in a surprise attack; on the same day they took it, opened the granary and ate freely, and within ten days they had more than two hundred thousand able soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi sent Ji with five thousand men to cross the Yellow River from Yuanwu in a surprise attack. They took the place the same day, opened the granaries, and within ten days had more than two hundred thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 經歲餘，宇文化及於江都弒逆，擁兵北上，直指東郡。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Yuwen Huaji committed regicide at Jiangdu, gathered troops and marched north, pointing straight at Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor at Jiangdu, gathered an army, and marched north toward Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時越王侗即位於東京，赦密之罪，拜為太尉，封魏國公；

translations.literal: At that time Prince Yue Yang Tong ascended the throne in the Eastern Capital, pardoned Mi's crimes, appointed him Grand Marshal, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue Yang Tong had then taken the throne in the Eastern Capital. He pardoned Mi, made him Grand Marshal, and created him Duke of Wei;

sentences.zh: 授勣右武候大將軍，命討化及。

translations.literal: Ji was appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and ordered to campaign against Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Ji grand general of the Right Martial Guard with orders to suppress Huaji.

sentences.zh: 密遣勣守倉城，勣於城外掘深溝以固守，化及設攻具，四面攻倉，阻塹不得至城下，勣於塹中為地道，出兵擊之，大敗而去。

translations.literal: Mi dispatched Ji to hold Cang City; Ji dug deep moats outside the city to hold firm. Huaji set up siege engines and attacked the granary from four sides, but was blocked by the moat and could not reach the foot of the wall; Ji made tunnels within the moat, sent troops out to strike, and greatly defeated him so that he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mi sent Ji to hold Cang City. Ji dug deep trenches outside the walls to stand firm. Huaji brought up siege engines and attacked from all sides, but the trenches kept him from the walls. Ji dug tunnels beneath the trenches, sallied out, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，密為王世充所破，擁眾歸朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, Mi was broken by Wang Shichong and came to court with his followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude, Wang Shichong broke Mi's force and Mi came over to the Tang with his followers.

sentences.zh: 其舊境東至於海，南至於江，西至汝州，北至魏郡，勣並據之，未有所屬，謂長史郭孝恪曰：「魏公既歸大唐，今此人眾土地，魏公所有也。

translations.literal: His former territory extended east to the sea, south to the Yangzi, west to Ru Prefecture, and north to Wei Commandery; Ji held it all and had not yet submitted to anyone. He said to Chief Administrator Guo Xiaoke, "Since Duke Wei has already returned to Great Tang, these people, territory, and lands now belong to Duke Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ji still held Mi's old domain, from the sea in the east to the Yangzi in the south, Ru Prefecture in the west, and Wei Commandery in the north, and had not yet declared for any side. He told his chief administrator Guo Xiaoke, "Since Duke Wei has submitted to Great Tang, these people and this land belong to him."

sentences.zh: 吾若上表獻之，即是利主之敗，自為己功，以邀富貴，吾所恥也。

translations.literal: If I submit a memorial offering them up, that would be profiting from my lord's defeat and making my own achievement to seek wealth and honor—this is what I would be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: If I memorialized the throne and offered it all up myself, I would be profiting from my lord's fall and claiming the credit to win rank and riches. That is what I would be ashamed to do.

sentences.zh: 今宜具錄州縣名數及軍人戶口，總啟魏公，聽公自獻，此則魏公之功也。

translations.literal: Now we should fully record the names and numbers of prefectures and counties and the households of soldiers and people, report all to Duke Wei, and let the Duke offer them himself—then this will be Duke Wei's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: We should instead record every prefecture, county, soldier, and household and report the whole to Duke Wei, so that he may present it himself. Then the merit will be his.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使啟密。

translations.literal: " He thereupon sent envoys to report to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent envoys to inform Mi.

sentences.zh: 使人初至，高祖聞其無表，惟有啟與密，甚怪之。

translations.literal: When the envoys first arrived, Gaozu heard that there was no memorial from him, only a report to Mi, and was greatly puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys first arrived, Gaozu was puzzled to find no memorial from Ji, only a report addressed to Mi.

sentences.zh: 使者以勣意聞奏，高祖大喜曰：「徐世勣感德推功，實純臣也。

translations.literal: The envoys reported Ji's intent to the throne; Gaozu was greatly pleased and said, "Xu Shiji, moved by virtue, pushes merit to another—he is truly a pure minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys explained Ji's intent, Gaozu was delighted and said, "Xu Shiji honors his lord and yields the credit. He is a minister of true integrity."

sentences.zh: 」詔授黎陽總管、上柱國，萊國公。

translations.literal: " An edict appointed him Area Commander of Liyang, Upper Pillar of State, and Duke of Lai.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict made him area commander of Liyang, Upper Pillar of State, and Duke of Lai.

sentences.zh: 尋加右武候大將軍，改封曹國公，賜姓李氏，賜良田五十頃，甲第一區。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard, re-enfeoffed as Duke of Cao, granted the surname Li, and given fifty qing of good farmland and one first-class mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made grand general of the Right Martial Guard, re-created Duke of Cao, granted the imperial surname Li, and given fifty qing of good land and a first-rank mansion.

sentences.zh: 封其父蓋為濟陰王，蓋固辭王爵，乃封舒國公，授散騎常侍、陵州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Gai was enfeoffed as King of Jiyin; Gai firmly declined the royal title, and so was enfeoffed as Duke of Shu and appointed Palace Attendant and Governor of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gai was created King of Jiyin, but Gai firmly refused a royal title and accepted instead the dukedom of Shu, with appointment as palace attendant and governor of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 令勣總統河南、山東之兵以拒王世充。

translations.literal: Ji was ordered to command all troops of Henan and Shandong to resist Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was placed in overall command of the armies of Henan and Shandong to hold Wang Shichong at bay.

sentences.zh: 及李密反叛伏誅，高祖以勣舊經事密，遣使報其反狀。

translations.literal: When Li Mi rebelled and was executed, Gaozu, because Ji had formerly served under Mi, sent envoys to report Mi's act of rebellion to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi rebelled and was executed, Gaozu, knowing Ji had once served under him, sent envoys to inform him of Mi's treason.

sentences.zh: 勣表請收葬，詔許之。

translations.literal: Ji submitted a memorial requesting permission to gather and bury him; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji petitioned for permission to bury Mi properly, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 勣服衰絰，與舊僚吏將士葬密於黎山之南，墳高七仞，釋服而散，朝野義之。

translations.literal: Ji wore mourning garments, and together with former subordinate officials, officers, and soldiers buried Mi south of Mount Li; the mound was seven ren high. After removing mourning dress they dispersed, and court and country praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ji put on mourning dress and, with Mi's old officers and men, buried him south of Mount Li in a mound seven ren high. When the rites were done they dispersed, and all who heard of it praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而竇建德擒化及於魏縣，復進軍攻勣，力屈降之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Dou Jiande captured Huaji at Wei County, then advanced again to attack Ji; exhausted in strength, Ji surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Dou Jiande captured Huaji at Wei County, then marched against Ji and forced him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 建德收其父，從軍為質，令勣復守黎陽。

translations.literal: Jiande took his father, kept him with the army as hostage, and ordered Ji again to hold Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande took Ji's father hostage with the army and ordered Ji back to the defense of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 三年，自拔歸京師。

translations.literal: In the third year he broke out on his own and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he broke free and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，從太宗伐王世充於東都，累戰大捷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Taizong in campaigning against Wang Shichong at the Eastern Capital and repeatedly fought to great victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Taizong against Wang Shichong at the Eastern Capital and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 又東略地至武牢，偽鄭州司兵沈悅請翻武牢，勣夜潛兵應接，克之。

translations.literal: He also marched east to seize territory as far as Wulao; Shen Yue, Military Registrar of the false Zheng Prefecture, requested to turn Wulao over, and Ji by night secretly sent troops to link up with him and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He also pushed east as far as Wulao. Shen Yue, registrar of the Zheng army, offered to turn the fortress, and Ji sent troops by night to meet him and took the place.

sentences.zh: 擒其偽刺史荊王行本。

translations.literal: He captured the false prefect, Prince Jing Xingben.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Zheng prefect, Prince Jing Xingben.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗平竇建德，降王世充，振旅而還。

translations.literal: He again followed Taizong in pacifying Dou Jiande and accepting Wang Shichong's surrender, then returned with the army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Taizong in defeating Dou Jiande and accepting Wang Shichong's surrender, and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 論功行賞，太宗為上將，勣為下將，與太宗俱服金甲，乘戎輅，告捷於太廟。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed and rewards distributed, Taizong served as upper commander and Ji as lower commander; together with Taizong he wore golden armor, rode the war chariot, and reported victory at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were given for merit, Taizong took the place of upper commander and Ji that of lower commander. Together in golden armor they rode the war chariot to report victory at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 其父自洺州與裴矩入朝，高祖見之大喜，復其官爵。

translations.literal: His father came from Ming Prefecture to court together with Pei Ju; Gaozu saw him and was greatly pleased, and restored his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: His father came to court from Ming Prefecture with Pei Ju. Gaozu was delighted to see him and restored his office and noble title.

sentences.zh: 勣又從太宗破劉黑闥、徐圓朗，累遷左監門大將軍。

translations.literal: Ji again followed Taizong in defeating Liu Heita and Xu Yuanlang, and was repeatedly promoted to General of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ji again served under Taizong against Liu Heita and Xu Yuanlang and rose by stages to general of the left gate guard.

sentences.zh: 圓朗重據兗州反，授勣河南大總管以討之，尋獲圓朗，斬首以獻，兗州平。

translations.literal: Yuanlang again seized Yanzhou and rebelled; Ji was appointed Grand Commander of Henan to suppress him. Soon he captured Yuanlang, beheaded him and presented the head, and Yanzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanlang again seized Yanzhou and rebelled, Ji was made grand commander of Henan to put him down. He soon captured Yuanlang, sent his head as tribute, and Yanzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔與趙郡王孝恭討輔公祏，孝恭領舟師巡江而下，勣領步卒一萬渡淮，拔其壽陽，至硤石。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict ordered him together with Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong to campaign against Fu Gongshi. Xiaogong led the fleet downstream along the river; Ji led ten thousand infantry across the Huai, captured their Shouyang, and reached Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was ordered with Prince Xiaogong of Zhao to campaign against Fu Gongshi. Xiaogong led the fleet downriver while Ji crossed the Huai with ten thousand foot soldiers, took Shouyang, and advanced to Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 公祏之將陳正通率兵十萬屯於梁山，又遣其大將馮惠亮帥水軍十萬，鎖連大艦以斷江路，仍於江西結壘，分守水陸，以御王師。

translations.literal: Gongshi's general Chen Zhengtong led a hundred thousand troops and encamped at Liangshan. He also sent his great general Feng Huiliang to command a hundred thousand naval troops, chaining together great ships to block the river route; moreover he built fortified camps west of the river, dividing defense between land and water to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi's general Chen Zhengtong encamped at Liangshan with a hundred thousand men. His commander Feng Huiliang brought another hundred thousand sailors, chained great warships across the river, and built fortifications on the west bank to hold both land and water against the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 勣攻其壘，尋克之。

translations.literal: Ji attacked their fortified camp and soon captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji stormed the fort and took it shortly thereafter.

sentences.zh: 惠亮單舼而遁。

translations.literal: Huiliang fled in a lone boat.
translations.idiomatic: Huiliang escaped alone in a small boat.

sentences.zh: 勣乘勝逼正通，大潰，以十餘騎奔於丹陽。

translations.literal: Ji pressed the advantage against Zhengtong; the enemy suffered a great rout, and with a dozen or so horsemen fled to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji pressed the victory against Zhengtong and routed his force. Zhengtong fled to Danyang with barely a dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 公祐棄城夜遁，勣縱騎追斬之於武康，江南悉定。
