translations.literal: Gongshi abandoned the city and fled by night; Ji let loose cavalry in pursuit and cut him down at Wukang; all south of the Yangtze was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi abandoned his city and fled under cover of night. Ji sent cavalry in pursuit and killed him at Wukang, and all of Jiangnan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 八年，突厥寇并州，命勣為行軍總管，擊之於太谷，走之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Turks raided Bing Prefecture. Ji was appointed campaign commander, struck them at Taigu, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Turks raided Bingzhou, Ji was made campaign commander, defeated them at Taigu, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，拜并州都督，賜實封九百戶。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded to the throne, Ji was appointed Military Governor of Bing Prefecture and granted nine hundred taxable households in actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Ji was made military governor of Bingzhou and granted a fief of nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，為通漠道行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he served as campaign commander on the Tongmo Route.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 he was made commander of the campaign on the Tongmo route.

sentences.zh: 至雲中，與突厥頡利可汗兵會，大戰於白道。

translations.literal: Reaching Yunzhong, he joined battle with the Turk Jieli Khan's forces and fought a great battle on the White Route.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunzhong he met the army of the Turk khan Jieli and fought a major battle on the White Route.

sentences.zh: 突厥敗，屯營於磧口，遣使請和。

translations.literal: The Turks were defeated and encamped at Qikou, sending envoys to request peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were beaten and encamped at Qikou, where they sent envoys suing for peace.

sentences.zh: 詔鴻臚卿唐儉往赦之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Jian to go and pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Jian to grant them a pardon.

sentences.zh: 勣時與定襄道大總管李靖軍會，相與議曰：「頡利雖敗，人眾尚多，若走渡磧，保於九姓，道遙阻深，追則難及。

translations.literal: Ji at this time joined with Grand Commander of the Dingxiang Route Li Jing's army, and together they discussed, saying, "Although Jieli is defeated, his people are still numerous; if he flees across the desert and takes refuge among the Nine Surnames, the road will be distant and obstructed, and pursuit will be hard to overtake.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had joined Li Jing, grand commander on the Dingxiang route, and they discussed the situation: "Jieli is defeated, but his following is still large. If he crosses the desert and takes refuge with the Nine Surnames, the way will be long and hard, and we may not catch him.

sentences.zh: 今詔使唐儉至彼，其必弛備，我等隨後襲之，此不戰而平賊矣。

translations.literal: Now that the edict envoy Tang Jian has reached them, they will surely slacken their guard; we may follow close behind and strike them — thus the bandits may be pacified without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: With Tang Jian there on the emperor's mission, they will surely let down their guard. We can follow right behind and strike — and bring the foe to heel without a battle."

sentences.zh: 」靖扼腕喜曰：「公之此言，乃韓信滅田橫之策也。

translations.literal: Jing, clutching his wrist in delight, said, "Your words are the very strategy by which Han Xin destroyed Tian Heng!"
translations.idiomatic: Jing slapped his wrist and cried, "That is the very plan Han Xin used to destroy Tian Heng!"

sentences.zh: 」於是定計。

translations.literal: Thereupon they settled on a plan.
translations.idiomatic: They settled on the plan.

sentences.zh: 靖將兵逼夜而發，勣勒兵繼進。

translations.literal: Jing led his troops to set out at nightfall; Ji mustered troops and pressed on behind.
translations.idiomatic: Jing marched his men out at nightfall and Ji brought his army up behind.

sentences.zh: 靖軍既至，賊營大潰，頡利與萬餘人欲走渡磧。

translations.literal: When Jing's army arrived, the enemy camp was routed in great disorder; Jieli with more than ten thousand men wished to flee across the desert.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's army arrived, the enemy camp collapsed. Jieli and more than ten thousand men tried to flee across the desert.

sentences.zh: 勣屯軍於磧口，頡利至，不得渡磧，其大酋長率其部落並降於勣，虜五萬餘口而還。

translations.literal: Ji stationed troops at Qikou; when Jieli arrived he could not cross the desert. The great chieftains led their tribes all to surrender to Ji; he took more than fifty thousand captives and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ji blocked Qikou. When Jieli arrived he could not cross the desert, and the great chieftains brought their tribes to surrender to Ji. He took more than fifty thousand captives and returned.

sentences.zh: 時高宗為晉王，遙領并州大都督，授勣光祿大夫，行并州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: At this time Gaozong was Prince of Jin, holding from afar the post of Grand Military Governor of Bing Prefecture; Ji was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Acting Chief Administrator of the Bing Prefecture Grand Military Governorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gaozong, then Prince of Jin, was nominal grand military governor of Bingzhou. Ji was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and acting chief administrator of the Bingzhou governor's office.

sentences.zh: 父憂解，尋起復舊職。

translations.literal: On mourning for his father he was released from office; soon he was recalled to resume his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his father, then was soon recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 十一年，改封英國公，代襲蘄州刺史，時並不就國，復以本官遙領太子左衛率。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Ying, hereditarily succeeding as Governor of Qi Prefecture; at the time he went to neither fief, but again with his original office held from afar the post of Left Defender of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was created Duke of Ying and was also to inherit the governorship of Qizhou in succession, but he took up neither post and remained at Bingzhou while also serving as left defender of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 勣在并州凡十六年，令行禁止，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Ji was at Bing Prefecture altogether sixteen years; orders went forth and prohibitions stood — he was praised as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Ji spent sixteen years at Bingzhou. His rule was firm and effective, and he was counted a capable governor.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂侍臣曰：「隋煬帝不能精選賢良，安撫邊境，惟解築長城以備突厥，情識之惑，一至於此！

translations.literal: Taizong said to his attending ministers: "Emperor Yang of Sui could not carefully select the worthy and good and pacify the frontiers — he understood only building the Long Wall to guard against the Turks; the delusion of mind and perception reached this extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told his ministers, "Emperor Yang of Sui could not choose worthy men or secure the frontiers — he knew only to build the Long Wall against the Turks. What a folly of judgment!

sentences.zh: 朕今委任李世勣於并州，遂使突厥畏威遁走，塞垣安靜，豈不勝遠築長城耶？」

translations.literal: I now entrust Li Shiji to Bing Prefecture, and thereby make the Turks fear our might and flee away; the frontier passes are peaceful — is this not better than building the Long Wall from afar?"
translations.idiomatic: By placing Li Shiji at Bingzhou I have made the Turks fear our power and withdraw, and the frontier is quiet. Is that not better than building a distant wall?"

sentences.zh: 十五年，徵拜兵部尚書，未赴京，會薛延陀遣其子大度設帥騎八萬南侵李思摩部落。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of War; before he reached the capital, the Xueyantuo sent the khan's son Dadu She at the head of eighty thousand horsemen to invade south against the Li Simo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was summoned as Minister of War. Before he reached the capital, the Xueyantuo sent the khan's son Dadushe south with eighty thousand horsemen against Li Simo's tribe.

sentences.zh: 命勣為朔州行軍總管，率輕騎三千追及延陀於青山，擊大破之，斬其名王一人，俘獲首領，虜五萬餘計，以功封一子為縣公。

translations.literal: Ji was ordered as campaign commander of Shuozhou; with three thousand light cavalry he pursued and caught the Xueyantuo at Qingshan, struck and routed them greatly, beheaded one of their titled kings, captured leaders, and took more than fifty thousand captives; for his merit one son was enfeoffed as Duke of a county.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was made campaign commander at Shuozhou. With three thousand light cavalry he caught the Xueyantuo at Qingshan, routed them, killed one of their titled princes, seized many leaders, and took more than fifty thousand captives. For this he had one son enfeoffed as a county duke.

sentences.zh: 勣時遇暴疾，驗方云，鬚灰可以療之，太宗乃自翦鬚，為其和藥。

translations.literal: Ji at this time suffered a sudden violent illness; according to tested prescriptions, beard ash could cure it. Taizong thereupon cut his own beard and mixed medicine with it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji fell suddenly ill. According to a tested prescription, beard ash could cure the ailment, so Taizong cut his own beard and mixed it into the medicine.

sentences.zh: 勣頓首見血，泣以懇謝，帝曰：「吾為社稷計耳，不煩深謝。

translations.literal: Ji bowed until his forehead bled, weeping in earnest gratitude. The emperor said, "I did it for the sake of the state — no need for deep thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Ji kowtowed until his forehead bled and wept his thanks. The emperor said, "I did it for the realm. Do not thank me overmuch.

sentences.zh: 」十七年，高宗為皇太子，轉勣太子詹事兼左衛率，加位特進，同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Gaozong became Crown Prince, Ji was transferred to be Counselor of the Crown Prince and concurrently Left Defender, promoted to Special Advance, and made of equal rank with the Three Chiefs of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when Gaozong became crown prince, Ji was made counselor to the crown prince and left defender, promoted to special advance, and accorded third-rank standing with the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「我兒新登儲貳，卿舊長史，今以宮事相委，故有此授。

translations.literal: Taizong said to him: "My son has newly ascended as heir apparent; you were formerly his chief administrator — I now entrust palace affairs to you, hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told him, "My son is newly made heir, and you were once his chief administrator. I am entrusting the palace to you — hence this appointment.

sentences.zh: 雖屈階資，可勿怪也。

translations.literal: Although it may seem to reduce your rank and seniority, do not take offense."
translations.idiomatic: It may seem a demotion in rank, but do not be offended."

sentences.zh: 」太宗又嘗閒宴，顧勣曰：「朕將屬以幼孤，思之無越卿者。

translations.literal: Taizong also once at a leisurely banquet turned to Ji and said, "I am about to entrust my young orphan to you; thinking it over, there is no one better than you.
translations.idiomatic: At another informal banquet Taizong turned to Ji and said, "I mean to entrust my young heir to you, and I can think of no one better.

sentences.zh: 公往不遺於李密，今豈負於朕哉！

translations.literal: You did not fail Li Mi in the past — how could you fail me now!"
translations.idiomatic: You did not fail Li Mi. How could you fail me now!"

sentences.zh: 」勣雪涕致辭，因噬指流血。

translations.literal: Ji, tears streaming, made his reply, and biting his finger drew blood.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wept as he answered and bit his finger until it bled.

sentences.zh: 俄而沉醉，乃解御服覆之，其見委信如此。

translations.literal: Before long he was deeply drunk; Taizong thereupon removed his own imperial robes to cover him — such was the trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon drank himself into a stupor, and Taizong took off his own robe to cover him — such was the trust he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 十八年，太宗將親征高麗，授勣遼東道行軍大總管，攻破蓋牟、遼東、白崖等數城，又從太宗摧殄駐蹕陣，以功封一子為郡公。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Taizong was about to campaign in person against Goguryeo; Ji was appointed Grand Campaign Commander of the Liaodong Route, captured several cities including Gaimou, Liaodong, and Baiya, and also followed Taizong in crushing the Zhupi Array; for his merit one son was enfeoffed as Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Taizong prepared to lead a personal campaign against Goguryeo. Ji was made grand commander on the Liaodong route, took several cities including Gaimou, Liaodong, and Baiya, and helped Taizong break the Zhupi line. One son was enfeoffed as a commandery duke for his service.

sentences.zh: 二十年，延陀部落擾亂，詔勣將二百騎便發突厥兵討擊。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the Xueyantuo tribes were in disorder; an edict ordered Ji to take two hundred horsemen and promptly raise Turk troops to attack and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the Xueyantuo tribes fell into turmoil. Ji was ordered to take two hundred horsemen and immediately mobilize Turk forces against them.

sentences.zh: 至烏德鞬山，大戰破之。

translations.literal: Reaching Mount Wudejian, he fought a great battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Wudejian he fought a great battle and routed them.

sentences.zh: 其大首領梯真達於率眾來防，其可汗咄摩支南竄於荒谷，遣通事舍人蕭嗣業招慰部領，送於京師，磧北悉定。

translations.literal: Their great chieftain Tizhen Dayu led the multitude to come and defend; their khan Duomozhi fled south into a desolate valley. Ji dispatched Interpreter-in-Attendance Xiao Siye to summon and reassure the tribes, sent them to the capital, and all north of the desert was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Their great chieftain Tizhen Dayu came out to oppose him, while their khan Duomozhi fled south into a wild ravine. Ji sent the interpreter-attendant Xiao Siye to win over the tribal leaders and escort them to the capital, and all north of the desert was pacified.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，轉太常卿，仍同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies, still of equal rank with the Three Chiefs of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became minister of ceremonies while retaining third-rank standing with the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 旬日，復除太子詹事。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was again appointed Counselor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he was again made counselor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，太宗寢疾，謂高宗曰：「汝於李勣無恩，我今將責出之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Taizong lay ill and said to Gaozong: "You owe Li Ji no favor; I shall now dismiss him and send him away.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, as Taizong lay ill, he told Gaozong, "You owe Li Ji nothing. I am going to demote him and send him away.

sentences.zh: 我死後，汝當授以僕射，即荷汝恩，必致其死力。

translations.literal: After I die, you should appoint him as Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; then, bearing your favor, he will surely exert himself unto death."
translations.idiomatic: After I die, promote him to vice director. Grateful for your favor, he will give you his utmost loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」乃出為疊州都督。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Military Governor of Die Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was then sent out as military governor of Diezhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，其月，召拜洛州刺史，尋加開府儀同三司，令同中書門下，參掌機密。

translations.literal: When Gaozong acceded to the throne, that same month Ji was summoned and appointed Governor of Luo Prefecture; soon he was also given the title of Honorary Grand General of the State Secretariat with Third-Rank Honors, ordered to serve with the Secretariat and Chancellery and share in handling state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne, he summoned Ji that same month as governor of Luozhou, soon added the title of honorary grand general of third rank, and put him among the chancellors to share in state secrets.

sentences.zh: 是歲，冊拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed by patent as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was formally appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，抗表求解僕射，仍令以開府儀同三司依舊知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he submitted a memorial refusing the vice directorship, but was still ordered to continue handling state affairs as Honorary Grand General with Third-Rank Honors.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 1 he petitioned to resign as vice director but was kept in office with his honorary third-rank title and duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 四年，冊拜司空。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed by patent as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀中，太宗以勳庸特著，嘗圖其形於凌煙閣，至是，帝又命寫形焉，仍親為之序。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Zhenguan, because his merit was especially outstanding Taizong had once painted his likeness in Lingyan Pavilion; at this time the emperor again ordered his likeness painted and personally wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Zhenguan, Taizong had placed Ji's portrait in the Lingyan Pavilion for his extraordinary service. Now the emperor ordered a new portrait and wrote the inscription himself.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，從幸東都，在路遇疾，帝親臨問。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing he followed the emperor in visiting the Eastern Capital; on the road he fell ill, and the emperor came in person to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 3, while accompanying the emperor to the eastern capital, he fell ill on the road and the emperor visited him in person.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，東封泰山，詔勣為封禪大使，乃從駕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longde, when the eastern feng-shan rite was performed at Mount Tai, an edict appointed Ji as envoy for the feng-shan ceremony, and he accompanied the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Longde era, when the emperor went east to perform the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai, Ji was made envoy for the ceremony and joined the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 次滑州，其姊早寡，居勣舊閭，皇后親自臨問，賜以衣服，仍封為東平郡君。

translations.literal: When they stopped at Hua Prefecture, his elder sister, long widowed, lived in Ji's old lane; the empress came in person to inquire after her, bestowed clothing, and enfeoffed her as Lady of Dongping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At Huazhou they paused. Ji's elder sister, long a widow, lived in his old neighborhood. The empress visited her in person, gave her clothing, and created her Lady of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 又墜馬傷足，上親降問，以所乘賜之。

translations.literal: Again he fell from a horse and injured his foot; the emperor came down in person to inquire, and bestowed upon him the mount he was riding.
translations.idiomatic: He also fell from his horse and hurt his foot. The emperor came to inquire in person and gave him the horse he had been riding.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，高麗莫離支男產為其弟男建所逐，保於國內城，遣子獻城詣闕乞師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng, Goguryeo's Molichi Nanchan was driven out by his younger brother Nangian, took refuge in the inner fortress of the capital, and sent his son to surrender the fortress and come to court seeking troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfeng 1, Goguryeo's Nanchan was expelled by his brother Nangian and shut himself in the inner citadel. He sent his son to surrender the city and seek aid at court.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，命勣為遼東道行軍總管，率兵二萬略地至鴨綠水。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang Ji was ordered as campaign commander of the Liaodong Route, leading twenty thousand troops in raiding to the Yalu River.
translations.idiomatic: In Zongzhang 1 Ji was made commander on the Liaodong route and led twenty thousand men in a sweep to the Yalu River.

sentences.zh: 賊遣其弟來拒戰，勣縱兵擊敗之，追奔二百里，至於平壤城。

translations.literal: The enemy sent Nangian's younger brother to meet battle; Ji let loose his troops, defeated him, pursued the rout two hundred li, and reached Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent Nangian's brother to fight. Ji routed him, pursued the fleeing army two hundred li, and reached Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 男建閉門不敢出，賊中諸城駭懼，多拔人眾遁走，降款者相繼。

translations.literal: Nangian closed the gates and dared not come out; cities throughout the enemy territory were terrified, many uprooted their people and fled, and those submitting came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Nangian shut the gates and would not come out. Cities across Goguryeo panicked; many emptied their populations in flight, and surrender followed surrender.

sentences.zh: 勣又引兵圍平壤，遼東道副大總管劉仁軌、郝處俊、將軍薛仁貴並會於平壤，犄角圍之。

translations.literal: Ji again led troops to besiege Pyongyang; Deputy Grand Commander of the Liaodong Route Liu Rengui, Hao Chujun, and General Xue Rengui all converged at Pyongyang and from horns and corners jointly besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then invested Pyongyang. Liu Rengui and Hao Chujun, deputy grand commanders on the Liaodong route, and General Xue Rengui joined him there and pressed the siege from all sides.

sentences.zh: 經月餘，克其城，虜其王高藏及男建、男產，裂其諸城，並為州縣，振旅而旋。

translations.literal: After more than a month they captured the city, took captive their king Go Jang and Nangian and Nanchan, divided their various cities, all making them prefectures and counties, and returned in triumph with the army.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month they took the city, captured King Go Jang along with Nangian and Nanchan, carved the conquered territory into prefectures and counties, and marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 令勣便道以高藏及男建獻於昭陵，禮畢，備軍容入京城，獻太廟。

translations.literal: Ji was ordered by a convenient route to present Go Jang and Nangian at Zhaoling; when the ceremony was complete, in full military array he entered the capital and presented them at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was ordered to present Go Jang and Nangian at Zhaoling by a direct route. When the rite was done he entered the capital in full martial array and offered the captives at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 二年，加太子太師，增食實封通前一千一百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, and his taxable fief households were increased to eleven hundred in all including previous grants.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made grand preceptor to the crown prince and his fief was increased to eleven hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 其年寢疾，詔以勣為司衛正卿，使得視疾。

translations.literal: That year he lay bedridden with illness; an edict appointed him Director of the Directorate for Palace Guards and granted him leave to convalesce.
translations.idiomatic: That year he fell bedridden with illness. An edict made him director of the palace guards and granted him leave to convalesce.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，年七十六。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 帝為之舉哀，輟朝七日，贈太尉、揚州大都督，謚曰貞武，給東園秘器，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned for him, suspended court for seven days, posthumously awarded him Grand Preceptor and Grand Military Governor of Yangzhou, gave the posthumous title Zhenwu, granted Eastern Garden secret funerary objects, and ordered burial at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, suspended court for seven days, posthumously created him grand preceptor and grand military governor of Yangzhou with the posthumous title Zhenwu, granted the Eastern Garden funerary regalia, and had him buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 令司平太常伯楊昉攝同文正卿監護。

translations.literal: He ordered Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Yang Fang to serve as acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to supervise the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Fang, vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices, to serve as acting director and supervise the funeral.

sentences.zh: 及葬日，帝幸未央古城，登樓臨送，望柳車慟哭，並為設祭。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the emperor visited the old city of Weiyang, ascended a tower to see him off, gazed at the willow-bedecked bier and wailed in grief, and also set out sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial the emperor went to the old city of Weiyang, climbed a tower to see him off, gazed at the willow-draped bier and wept aloud, and set out offerings.

sentences.zh: 皇太子亦從駕臨送，哀慟悲感左右。

translations.literal: The crown prince also followed the procession to see him off; his grief moved all those around him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince also joined the procession to see him off, and his grief moved all who were present.

sentences.zh: 詔百官送至故城西北，所築墳一准衛、霍故事，象陰山、鐵山及烏德鞬山，以旌破突厥、薛延陀之功。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to escort the bier to the northwest of the old city. The tomb mound built followed the precedent of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, shaped with likenesses of Mount Yin, Mount Tie, and Mount Wudejian to commemorate victories over the Turks and Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all officials to escort the bier to the northwest of the old city. The tomb mound followed the precedent of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, with likenesses of Mount Yin, Mount Tie, and Mount Wudejian to honor his victories over the Turks and Xueyantuo.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，詔勣配享高宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzai an edict ordered Ji to share offerings in the temple court of Gaozong's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzai 1 an edict ordered Ji to share offerings in Gaozong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 勣前後戰勝所得金帛，皆散之於將士。

translations.literal: All gold and silks Ji obtained from victories before and after he distributed among officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: All the gold and silk Ji won in battle he distributed among his officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 初得黎陽倉，就倉者數十萬人。

translations.literal: When he first took the Liyang granary, those who came to the granary numbered hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took the Liyang granary, hundreds of thousands came to its stores.

sentences.zh: 魏徵、高季輔、杜正倫、郭孝恪皆游其所，一見於眾人中，即加禮敬，引之臥內，談謔忘倦。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng, Gao Jifu, Du Zhenglun, and Guo Xiaoge all visited his quarters; upon seeing them once among the multitude he at once showed them courtesy and respect, brought them into his inner chamber, and talked and jested without wearying.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng, Gao Jifu, Du Zhenglun, and Guo Xiaoge all visited him. Spotting them in a crowd he would at once show them honor, bring them to his private chamber, and talk and jest with them far into the night.

sentences.zh: 及平武牢，獲偽鄭州長史戴胄，知其行能，尋釋於竟，推薦咸至顯達，當時稱其有知人之鑑。

translations.literal: When Wugao was pacified he captured the false Zheng state's Chief Administrator of Zheng Prefecture Dai Zhou; recognizing his conduct and ability, he soon released him completely, recommended him, and all reached eminence; the age praised his discernment in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: When Wugao fell he captured Dai Zhou, chief administrator of Zheng under the Zheng regime. Recognizing his talent, he soon released him and recommended him for office; all rose to prominence, and men praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 又，初平王世充，獲其故人單雄信，依例處死，勣表稱其武藝絕倫，若收之於合死之中，必大感恩，堪為國家盡命，請以官爵贖之。

translations.literal: Again, when Wang Shichong was first pacified, he captured his old friend Shan Xiongxin, who by precedent was to be executed. Ji submitted a memorial saying his martial skill was unmatched; if received from amid deserving death he would be deeply grateful and could devote his life to the state — requesting to redeem him with office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when Wang Shichong was first defeated he captured his old friend Shan Xiongxin, who by precedent was to be executed. Ji petitioned that Xiongxin's martial skill was unmatched, that if spared from death he would be deeply grateful and serve the state with his life, and asked to redeem him with office and rank.

sentences.zh: 高祖不許，臨將就戮，勣對之號慟，割股肉以啖之，曰：「生死永訣，此肉同歸於土矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu did not permit it. As execution was about to take place Ji faced him wailing in grief, cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to him, saying, "Life and death are parted forever; this flesh shall return to earth together.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused. As Xiongxin was about to be executed, Ji wept before him, cut flesh from his own thigh and fed it to him, saying, "We part forever in life and death; let this flesh return to earth together.

sentences.zh: 」仍收養其子。

translations.literal: He still took in and raised his son.
translations.idiomatic: He also took in and raised Xiongxin's son.

sentences.zh: 每行軍用師，頗任籌算，臨敵應變，動合事機。

translations.literal: Whenever he marched and employed armies he relied considerably on planning and calculation; facing the enemy he adapted to change, and his movements always matched the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he took the field he relied heavily on calculation; facing the enemy he adapted swiftly, and his moves always fit the moment.

sentences.zh: 與人圖計，識其臧否，聞其片善，扼腕而從。

translations.literal: When plotting plans with others he knew their right and wrong; hearing even a fragment of good in them, he would clutch his wrist and follow it.
translations.idiomatic: When planning with others he could tell sound counsel from bad, and if he heard even a scrap of good sense he would seize upon it.

sentences.zh: 事捷之日，多推功於下，以是人皆為用，所向多克捷。

translations.literal: On days when affairs succeeded he often pushed merit down to subordinates; thus everyone was willing to serve him, and wherever he turned there was often victory.
translations.idiomatic: When victory came he often gave the credit to his subordinates, so that all were eager to serve him and his campaigns usually succeeded.

sentences.zh: 洎勣之死，聞者莫不淒愴。

translations.literal: By the time of Ji's death, all who heard of it were without exception grief-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji died, all who heard the news were deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 與弟弼特存友愛，閨門之內，肅若嚴君。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Bi he especially preserved brotherly affection; within the inner quarters he was solemn as a strict father.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to his younger brother Bi, and within the household he was as stern as a strict father.

sentences.zh: 自遇疾，高宗及皇太子送藥，即取服之；

translations.literal: From the time he fell ill, when Gaozong and the crown prince sent medicine he at once took and swallowed it;
translations.idiomatic: From the time he fell ill, whenever Gaozong and the crown prince sent medicine he took it at once;

sentences.zh: 家中召醫巫，皆不許入門。

translations.literal: if the household summoned physicians or shamans he did not permit them to enter the gate.
translations.idiomatic: but if the household called in physicians or shamans he would not let them through the gate.

sentences.zh: 子弟固以藥進，勣謂曰：「我山東一田夫耳，攀附明主，濫居富貴，位極三台，年將八十，豈非命乎？

translations.literal: When sons and younger brothers firmly pressed medicine upon him, Ji said, "I am but a peasant from east of the mountains; clinging to a wise lord I undeservedly dwell in wealth and honor, rank reaching the Three Platforms, age nearing eighty — is this not fate?
translations.idiomatic: When his sons pressed medicine on him, Ji said, "I am only a farmer from Shandong who clung to a wise sovereign and undeservedly rose to the highest rank, nearly eighty years old. Is this not heaven's decree?

sentences.zh: 修短必是有期，寧容浪就醫人求活！

translations.literal: Long and short life must have their term — how could one lightly go to physicians begging to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Life and death have their appointed span. Why should I beg doctors for more time!"

sentences.zh: 」竟拒而不進。

translations.literal: In the end he refused and would not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused and would not take it.

sentences.zh: 忽謂弼曰：「我似得小差，可置酒以申宴樂。

translations.literal: Suddenly he said to Bi, "I seem to have a slight improvement; we may set out wine to express feast and joy."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he told Bi, "I think I am a little better. Let us set out wine and make merry."

sentences.zh: 」於是堂上奏女妓，簷下列子孫。

translations.literal: Thereupon female performers played in the hall, and below the eaves sons and grandchildren were arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians played in the hall while his sons and grandchildren lined up beneath the eaves.

sentences.zh: 宴罷，謂弼曰：「我自量必死，欲與汝一別耳。

translations.literal: When the feast ended he said to Bi, "I measure that I must die; I wished only to bid you farewell."
translations.idiomatic: When the feast was over he told Bi, "I know I am dying and only wanted to say goodbye.

sentences.zh: 恐汝悲哭，誑言似差，可未須啼泣，聽我約束。

translations.literal: Fearing you would weep in grief I lied that I seemed improved — you need not weep yet; listen to my instructions."
translations.idiomatic: I lied about feeling better because I feared your tears. Do not weep yet — hear my last commands."

sentences.zh: 我見房玄齡、杜如晦、高季輔辛苦作得門戶，亦望垂裕後昆，並遭痴兒破家蕩盡。

translations.literal: I have seen Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Gao Jifu labor painfully to build up their houses, likewise hoping to enrich their descendants — all suffered foolish sons to ruin their families and squander everything.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Gao Jifu painstakingly build up their houses and hope to leave comfort to their heirs — only to have witless sons squander everything.

sentences.zh: 我有如許豚犬，將以付汝，汝可防察，有操行不倫、交遊非類，急即打殺，然後奏知。

translations.literal: I have so many piglings and pups; I shall entrust them to you. You must guard and watch them: any whose conduct is improper or who consort with the wrong sort — immediately beat them to death, then report it."
translations.idiomatic: I have so many worthless sons. I leave them to you. Watch them closely: if any behaves disgracefully or keeps bad company, kill him at once and then report it."

sentences.zh: 又見人多埋金玉，亦不須爾。

translations.literal: Again, I see many people bury gold and jade — you need not do that either.
translations.idiomatic: And do not bury gold and jade in my grave, as so many do.

sentences.zh: 惟以布裝露車，載我棺柩，棺中斂以常服，惟加朝服一副，死倘有知，望著此奉見先帝。

translations.literal: Only use a cloth-covered open cart to carry my coffin; enclose me in the coffin in ordinary dress, adding only one set of court robes — if the dead have awareness, I hope to wear these when I go to meet the former emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Carry my coffin only on a plain cart draped in cloth. Dress me in ordinary clothes with one court robe added, so that if the dead have awareness I may wear them to greet the late emperor."

sentences.zh: 明器惟作馬五六匹，下帳用幔布為頂，白紗為裙，其中著十個木人，示依古禮芻靈之義，此外一物不用。

translations.literal: For mingqi make only five or six horses; for the lower canopy use curtain cloth for the top and white silk for the skirt, placing within ten wooden figures — showing accordance with the ancient rite of straw spirit-servants; beyond these use not a single thing more.
translations.idiomatic: For grave goods make only five or six horses. Let the lower canopy have a curtain-cloth top and white-silk sides, with ten wooden figures inside, following the ancient custom of straw spirit-servants. Use nothing else.

sentences.zh: 姬媼已下，有兒女而願住自養者，聽之；

translations.literal: Of concubines and nursemaids downward, those who have children and wish to remain to raise them on their own — permit it;
translations.idiomatic: As for concubines and nursemaids, if any have children and wish to stay and raise them, allow it;

sentences.zh: 余並放出。

translations.literal: All the rest release as well.
translations.idiomatic: Release all the rest as well.

sentences.zh: 事畢，汝即移入我堂，撫卹小弱。

translations.literal: When the affairs are finished, you shall at once move into my hall and comfort and succor the young and weak.
translations.idiomatic: When all is done, move into my hall at once and look after the women and children.

sentences.zh: 違我言者，同於戮屍。

translations.literal: Whoever disobeys my words is the same as one whose corpse is mutilated in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever defies my instructions shall be treated as though his corpse were hacked apart in punishment.

sentences.zh: 」此後略不復語，弼等遵行遺言。

translations.literal: After this he scarcely spoke again; Bi and the others carried out his dying instructions.
translations.idiomatic: After that he barely spoke again. Bi and the others carried out his final wishes.

sentences.zh: 勣少弟感，幼有志操。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Gan, while still young, had aspiration and moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Gan showed strong character even as a boy.

sentences.zh: 李密之敗也，陷於王世充，世充逼令以書召勣，感曰：「家兄立身，不虧名節，今已事主，君臣分定，決不以感造次改圖。

translations.literal: When Li Mi was defeated, [Ji] fell into Wang Shichong's hands; Shichong compelled [Gan] to write a letter summoning Ji. Gan said, "My elder brother establishes himself without failing in fame and integrity. He now already serves a lord; the division between ruler and subject is fixed. I will by no means because of Gan rashly change course."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi was defeated, Ji was captured by Wang Shichong, who forced Gan to write summoning Ji to surrender. Gan replied, "My elder brother stands on his reputation and will not betray his honor. He already serves a lord, and the bond between ruler and subject is settled. I will never use myself to make him abruptly change course."

sentences.zh: 」卒不肯。

translations.literal: In the end he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 世充怒，遂害焉，時年十五。

translations.literal: Shichong was enraged and thereupon killed him; he was then fifteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong flew into a rage and had him killed. He was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 勣長子震，顯慶初官至桂州刺史，先勣卒。

translations.literal: Ji's eldest son Zhen, at the beginning of Xianqing reached the office of Prefect of Guizhou; he died before Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's eldest son Zhen became Prefect of Guizhou early in the Xianqing era and died before Ji did.

sentences.zh: 勣孫敬業。

translations.literal: Ji's grandson Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's grandson was Sun Jingye.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，則天太后臨朝，既而廢帝為廬陵王，立相王為皇帝，而政由天后，諸武皆當權任，人情憤怨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong died, Empress Dowager Zetian held court. Soon she deposed the emperor as Prince of Luling, enthroned the Prince of Xiang as emperor, yet government was exercised by the Heavenly Empress; all the Wu clan held power and office, and popular sentiment was filled with anger and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozong's death, Empress Dowager Wu took control of the court. She soon deposed the emperor as Prince of Luling and enthroned the Prince of Xiang, but real power belonged to Wu. Members of the Wu clan held key posts, and public resentment ran deep.

sentences.zh: 時給事中唐之奇貶授括蒼令，長安主簿駱賓王貶授臨海丞，詹事司直杜求仁黝縣丞，敬業坐事左授柳州司馬，其弟盩啡令敬猷亦坐累左遷，俱在揚州。

translations.literal: At the time, Supervising Secretary Tang Zhiqi was demoted and appointed Magistrate of Kuocang; Chief Clerk of Chang'an Luo Binwang was demoted and appointed Assistant Magistrate of Linhai; Direct Attendant of the Household Administration Du Qiuren was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of You County; Jingye, implicated in a matter, was demoted to left-hand Assistant in Liuzhou; his younger brother Jingyou, Magistrate of Zhoufei, was also implicated and demoted left — all were in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tang Zhiqi, a supervising secretary, had been demoted to magistrate of Kuocang; Luo Binwang, a chief clerk in Chang'an, to assistant magistrate of Linhai; Du Qiuren, a palace attendant, to assistant magistrate of You County; Jingye himself, punished for an offense, to assistant in Liuzhou; and his younger brother Jingyou, magistrate of Zhoufei, was implicated and demoted as well. All of them were in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬業用前盩啡尉魏思溫謀，據揚州。

translations.literal: Jingye employed the former Zhoufei Commandant Wei Siwen in plotting and seized Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye, aided by Wei Siwen, former commandant of Zhoufei, seized Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年七月，敬業遣其黨監察御史薛璋先求使江都，又令雍州人韋超詣璋告變，雲「揚州長史陳敬之與唐之奇謀逆」，璋乃收敬之系獄。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Sisheng, Jingye sent his follower Supervising Censor Xue Zhang first to seek assignment as envoy to Jiangdu, then ordered Wei Chao of Yong Province to go to Zhang and report a rebellion, saying "Yangzhou Chief Administrator Chen Jingzhi and Tang Zhiqi are plotting treason." Zhang thereupon arrested Jingzhi and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Sisheng, Jingye sent his follower, Supervising Censor Xue Zhang, to obtain a mission to Jiangdu, then had a man from Yongzhou named Wei Chao report to Zhang that "Yangzhou Chief Administrator Chen Jingzhi and Tang Zhiqi are plotting rebellion." Zhang thereupon arrested Jingzhi and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 居數日，敬業矯制殺敬之，自稱揚州司馬，詐言「高州首領馮子猷叛逆，奉密詔募兵進討。

translations.literal: After several days, Jingye forged an imperial order and killed Jingzhi, styled himself Assistant Administrator of Yangzhou, and falsely claimed, "The leader of Gaozhou, Feng Ziyou, has rebelled; following a secret edict I am recruiting troops to advance and suppress him."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Jingye forged an imperial order, executed Jingzhi, styled himself military adjutant of Yangzhou, and falsely announced, "Feng Ziyou, leader of Gaozhou, has rebelled. By secret edict I am raising troops to march against him."

sentences.zh: 」是日開府庫，令士曹參軍李宗臣解繫囚及丁役、工匠，得數百人，皆授之以甲。

translations.literal: That day he opened the storehouses, ordered Army Staff Officer Li Zongchen to release bound prisoners along with corvée laborers and craftsmen — obtaining several hundred men — and armed them all with armor.
translations.idiomatic: That day he opened the government stores, had army staff officer Li Zongchen free prisoners, conscript laborers, and craftsmen — several hundred men in all — and issued armor to each.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍孫處行拒命，敬業斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Recording Officer Sun Chuxing refused the order; Jingye beheaded him and displayed the head as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Recording officer Sun Chuxing refused. Jingye beheaded him and displayed the corpse as a warning.

sentences.zh: 遂據揚州，鳩聚民眾，以匡復廬陵為辭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized Yangzhou, gathered the people, and took as his stated cause the restoration of [the Prince of] Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He then held Yangzhou, gathered the people, and proclaimed the goal of restoring the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 乃開三府：一曰匡復府，二曰英公府，三曰揚州大都督府。

translations.literal: He then opened three offices: the first called the Office of Restoration, the second the Duke of Ying's Office, the third the Grand Governor-General's Office of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then established three headquarters: the Office of Restoration, the Duke of Ying's Office, and the Grand Military Headquarters of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬業自稱匡復府上將，領揚州大都督，以杜求仁、唐之奇、駱賓王為府屬，余皆偽署職位。

translations.literal: Jingye styled himself supreme general of the Office of Restoration and concurrently served as Grand Governor-General of Yangzhou; he made Du Qiuren, Tang Zhiqi, and Luo Binwang staff of the office, while all the rest received falsely appointed ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye styled himself supreme general of the Office of Restoration and commander of Yangzhou, appointed Du Qiuren, Tang Zhiqi, and Luo Binwang to his staff, and handed out the rest of the posts by false commission.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，勝兵有十餘萬。

translations.literal: Within ten days or so, battle-ready troops numbered more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days his effective forces swelled to more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 仍移檄諸郡縣曰：

translations.literal: He further issued a proclamation to the commanderies and counties, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a proclamation to the commanderies and counties:

sentences.zh: 偽臨朝武氏者，人非溫順，地實寒微。

translations.literal: The Wu clan woman who falsely holds court — her person is not gentle and compliant; her origin is truly humble and low.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu woman who has unlawfully seized the throne is neither gentle by nature nor noble in birth.

sentences.zh: 昔充太宗下陳，嘗以更衣入侍。

translations.literal: In former days she filled the rank of consort below Emperor Taizong, once entering attendance through changing of robes.
translations.idiomatic: Once she served among Emperor Taizong's junior consorts, attending him even during his changing of robes.

sentences.zh: 洎乎晚節，穢亂春宮。

translations.literal: Reaching her later years, she defiled and threw into disorder the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In her later years she corrupted the heir's palace with scandal.

sentences.zh: 密隱先帝之私，陰圖後庭之嬖。

translations.literal: She secretly concealed the former emperor's private affairs and covertly plotted for the favorites of the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: She concealed the late emperor's private affairs while secretly scheming for the favors of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 入門見嫉，蛾眉不肯讓人；

translations.literal: Upon entering the gate she was met with jealousy — arching brows unwilling to yield to others;
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had she entered the palace than her beauty provoked rivalry — those arched brows would yield to no rival;

sentences.zh: 掩袖工讒，狐媚偏能惑主。

translations.literal: Covering her sleeves she was skilled at slander; fox-like charm uniquely could bewitch the lord.
translations.idiomatic: She mastered the art of slander behind her sleeve; with foxlike allure she alone could bewitch her sovereign.

sentences.zh: 踐元後於翬翟，陷吾君於聚麀。

translations.literal: She trod upon the chief consort in pheasant-and-kingfisher regalia and trapped our lord in the offense of sharing one brood.
translations.idiomatic: She usurped the empress's place in full ceremonial dress and trapped our sovereign in the shame of sharing one household with a stepmother.

sentences.zh: 加以虺蠍為心，豺狼成性，近狎邪僻，殘害忠良，殺姊屠兄，弒君鴆母。

translations.literal: To this add a heart like serpent and scorpion, a nature formed like wolf and jackal — drawing close to the wicked and depraved, slaughtering the loyal and good, killing elder sisters and butchering elder brothers, regicide and poisoning mother.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, her heart is poison and her nature that of wolf and jackal. She keeps company with the wicked, destroys the loyal, murdered her elder sisters, slaughtered her brothers, and has even killed her sovereign and poisoned her mother.

sentences.zh: 人神之所同嫉，天地之所不容。

translations.literal: What gods and men alike detest; what heaven and earth cannot contain.
translations.idiomatic: She is hated by gods and men alike and cannot be tolerated by heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 猶復包藏禍心，窺竊神器。

translations.literal: Yet still she harbors a heart of calamity and stealthily covets the imperial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Even now she harbors treacherous intent and covets the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 君之愛子，幽之於別宮；

translations.literal: The lord's beloved son — she confines him in a separate palace;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's beloved son she has imprisoned in a distant palace;

sentences.zh: 賊之宗盟，委之以重任。

translations.literal: The rebel's clansmen and allies — to them she entrusts weighty responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: while she gives the rebels of her own clan the weightiest offices.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 霍子孟之不作，硃虛侯之已亡。

translations.literal: Huo Zimeng does not arise; the Marquis of Zhuxu is already gone.
translations.idiomatic: No Huo Guang rises to restore the throne; the Marquis of Zhuxu is long dead.

sentences.zh: 燕啄皇孫，知漢祚之將盡；

translations.literal: A swallow pecks at the imperial grandson — one knows the Han mandate is about to end;
translations.idiomatic: As when a swallow pecked the imperial grandson, we see the dynasty's mandate nearing its end;

sentences.zh: 龍漦帝后，識夏廷之遽衰。

translations.literal: Dragon spittle on the emperor's consort — one recognizes the Xia court's sudden decline.
translations.idiomatic: As when dragon spittle fell upon the empress, we know a dynasty's swift collapse when we see it.

sentences.zh: 敬業皇唐舊臣，公侯冢胤，奉先君之成業，荷本朝之舊恩。

translations.literal: Jingye, an old minister of mighty Tang, heir of duke and marquis, upholds his forebear's established enterprise and bears this dynasty's former grace.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye is an old servant of Tang, heir of a line of dukes and marquises, heir to his ancestors' achievements and bound by this court's ancient favors.

sentences.zh: 宋微子之興悲，良有以也；

translations.literal: When the Viscount of Wei of Song was moved to grief — truly there was reason for it;
translations.idiomatic: The grief of Weizi of Song had good cause;

sentences.zh: 袁君山之流涕，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: When Yuan Junshan shed tears — could it have been in vain!
translations.idiomatic: and Yuan Junshan's tears were not shed for nothing!

sentences.zh: 是用氣憤風雲，志安社稷，因天下之失望，順宇內之推心。

translations.literal: Therefore with spirit enraged at wind and clouds, will set to rest the altars of state — following the world's disappointment and accord with the heart the realm within the four seas puts forward.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore my spirit rises with the storm, and my purpose is to restore the realm — answering the world's disappointment and the heartfelt wish of all within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 爰舉義旗，誓清妖孽。

translations.literal: Hereby I raise the banner of righteousness and vow to sweep away evil demons.
translations.idiomatic: I now raise the banner of righteous revolt and swear to purge the realm of this evil.

sentences.zh: 南連百越，北盡三河，鐵騎成群，玉舳相接。

translations.literal: South joining the Hundred Yue, north reaching to the end of the Three Rivers — iron cavalry in throngs, jade-prowed ships linked one to another.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces link the southern Yue lands in the south and reach the Three Rivers in the north; iron cavalry stand in massed ranks, and polished warships lie hull to hull.

sentences.zh: 海陵紅粟，倉儲之積靡窮；

translations.literal: At Hailing, red grain — storehouse accumulations without end;
translations.idiomatic: At Hailing the granaries overflow with rice;

sentences.zh: 江浦黃旗，匡復之功何遠！

translations.literal: At the river's bank, yellow banners — how far off can the achievement of restoration be!
translations.idiomatic: and on the river's banks our yellow banners fly — how distant can restoration be!

sentences.zh: 班聲動而北風起，劍氣沖而南斗平。

translations.literal: When the sound of troops moves, the north wind rises; when sword aura shoots upward, the Southern Dipper is levelled.
translations.idiomatic: When our drums roll, the north wind rises; when our swords gleam, the southern stars tremble.

sentences.zh: 喑嗚則山嶽崩頹，叱咤則風雲變色。

translations.literal: A battle cry and mountains and peaks crumble; a shout and wind and clouds change color.
translations.idiomatic: Our war cry will shake the mountains; our shout will darken the sky.

sentences.zh: 以此制敵，何敵不摧？

translations.literal: With this to control the enemy — what enemy will not be shattered?
translations.idiomatic: With such a host, what foe can stand?

sentences.zh: 以此圖功，何功不克？

translations.literal: With this to plan achievement — what achievement will not be attained?
translations.idiomatic: With such an army, what goal cannot be won?

sentences.zh: 公等或家傳漢爵，或地協周親，或膺重寄於爪牙，或受顧命於宣室。

translations.literal: You, lords, some inherit Han enfeoffments from your families, some by territory match Zhou royal kin, some receive heavy trust as the ruler's claws and teeth, some received the dying charge in the Xuan Room.
translations.idiomatic: Some of you inherit Han-era titles; some share blood ties with the imperial house; some were entrusted as the emperor's right arm; some received the late emperor's final command in the Xuan Room.

sentences.zh: 言猶在耳，忠豈忘心？

translations.literal: His words are still in the ear — can loyalty be forgotten in the heart?
translations.idiomatic: His words still ring in your ears — can loyalty be forgotten?

sentences.zh: 一抔之土未乾，六尺之孤何托？

translations.literal: One handful of earth not yet dry — to whom can the six-foot orphan be entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: Before a single handful of earth has dried on the late emperor's tomb, to whom can his orphan son turn?

sentences.zh: 倘能轉禍為福，送往事居，共立勤王之師，無廢舊君之命，凡諸爵賞，同裂山河。

translations.literal: If you can turn calamity into blessing, escort the departed and serve the living, together raise an army to aid the emperor, and not abandon the mandate of the old sovereign — then for all ranks and rewards, you shall divide the mountains and rivers together.
translations.idiomatic: If you would turn disaster to blessing, honor the dead and serve the living, join us in raising an army to restore the throne and keep faith with the late emperor's will, every title and reward shall be shared among us as we carve up the realm.

sentences.zh: 請看今日之域中，竟是誰家之天下！

translations.literal: Behold in the realm today — in the end whose family's empire is it!
translations.idiomatic: Look upon the realm today and ask whose empire it has become!

sentences.zh: 則天命左玉鈐衛大將軍李孝逸將兵三十萬討之，追削敬業祖、父官爵，剖墳斫棺，復本姓徐氏。

translations.literal: Zetian ordered Left Jade Seal Guard General Li Xiaoyi to lead three hundred thousand troops to suppress them, posthumously stripped Jingye's grandfather and father of ranks and titles, exhumed their tombs and hacked open their coffins, and restored the original surname Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian ordered Left Jade Seal Guard General Li Xiaoyi to march against them with three hundred thousand men. She posthumously stripped Jingye's grandfather and father of rank, opened their graves and coffins, and restored the family's original surname of Xu.

sentences.zh: 初，敬業兵集，圖其所向，薛璋曰：「金陵王氣猶在，大江設險，可以自固。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jingye's army had assembled and they deliberated where to go, Xue Zhang said, "The kingly aura of Jinling is still present; the great river provides defenses — one can secure oneself there.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingye's forces first assembled and debated their direction, Xue Zhang said, "Jinling still holds royal auspice, and the Yangtze provides a natural barrier — we can make our stand there.

sentences.zh: 且取常、潤等州，以為霸基，然後治兵北渡。

translations.literal: Moreover seize Chang, Run, and other prefectures to serve as the foundation of hegemony, then drill troops and cross north."
translations.idiomatic: Seize Chang, Run, and the other prefectures to build our base, then train the army and cross north."

sentences.zh: 」魏思溫曰：「兵貴神速，但宜早渡淮而北，招合山東豪傑，乘其未集，直取東都，據關決戰，此上策也。

translations.literal: Wei Siwen said, "In warfare speed is precious; one should only cross the Huai early and go north, rally the eastern Shandong heroes, while the enemy has not yet assembled, strike straight for the eastern capital, hold the passes and fight the decisive battle — this is the superior strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Siwen said, "Speed is the soul of war. Cross the Huai at once and march north. Rally the magnates of Shandong, strike before the enemy gathers, seize the eastern capital, and hold the passes for the decisive battle. That is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 」敬業不從。

translations.literal: Jingye did not follow [their advice].
translations.idiomatic: Jingye refused.

sentences.zh: 十月，率眾渡江，攻拔潤州，殺刺史李思文。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he led the masses across the river, stormed and took Run Prefecture, and killed Prefect Li Siwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he crossed the Yangtze, captured Run Prefecture, and killed its prefect, Li Siwen.

sentences.zh: 先是，太子賢為天后所廢，死於巴州，敬業乃求狀貌似賢者，置於城中，奉之為主，雲賢本不死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Crown Prince Xian had been deposed by the Heavenly Empress and died in Bazhou. Jingye thereupon sought someone whose appearance resembled Xian's, placed him in the city, and honored him as lord, saying Xian had not died after all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Crown Prince Xian had been deposed by Wu and died in Bazhou. Jingye found a man who resembled him, installed him in the city, and proclaimed him ruler, claiming Xian had never died.

sentences.zh: 孝逸軍渡淮，至楚州，敬業之眾狼狽還江都，屯兵高郵以拒之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi's army crossed the Huai and reached Chuzhou. Jingye's forces fled in disorder back to Jiangdu and encamped at Gaoyou to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoyi's army crossed the Huai and reached Chuzhou. Jingye's beaten forces fled back to Jiangdu and made their stand at Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 頻戰大敗，孝逸乘勝追躡。

translations.literal: Repeated battles brought great defeat; Xiaoyi pursued pressing his victory.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats, Li Xiaoyi pressed his advantage in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 敬業奔至揚州，與唐之奇、杜求仁等乘小舸，將入海投高麗。

translations.literal: Jingye fled to Yangzhou; with Tang Zhiqi, Du Qiuren, and others he boarded a small boat, intending to enter the sea and flee to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye fled to Yangzhou and, with Tang Zhiqi, Du Qiuren, and others, took a small boat, intending to put to sea and seek refuge in Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 追兵及，皆捕獲之。

translations.literal: Pursuing troops caught up and all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers overtook them and took them all captive.

sentences.zh: 初，敬業傳檄至京師，則天讀之微哂，至「一抔之土未乾」，遽問侍臣曰：「此語誰為之？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jingye's proclamation reached the capital, Zetian read it with a faint smile; reaching "one handful of earth not yet dry," she abruptly asked the attending ministers, "Whose words are these?"
translations.idiomatic: When Jingye's proclamation first reached the capital, Wu read it with a faint smile — until she came to the line, "Before a single handful of earth has dried." She abruptly asked her ministers, "Who wrote this?"

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「駱賓王之辭也。

translations.literal: Someone answered, "It is the phrasing of Luo Binwang."
translations.idiomatic: One replied, "It is Luo Binwang's wording."

sentences.zh: 」則天曰：「宰相之過，安失此人？

translations.literal: Zetian said, "The chief ministers' fault — how did they let this man slip away?"
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, "That is the fault of the chief ministers — how could they have lost a man like this?"

sentences.zh: 」中宗返正，詔曰：「故司空勣，往因敬業，毀廢墳塋。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong returned to rightful rule, an edict said, "The late Grand Preceptor Ji, formerly because of Jingye, had his tomb and graveyard destroyed and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong was restored, an edict said, "The late Grand Preceptor Ji, because of Jingye's rebellion, had his tomb violated.

sentences.zh: 朕追想元勳，永懷佐命。

translations.literal: We recall the founding merit and ever cherish his assistance in receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: We recall his founding service and always remember his aid in establishing the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 昔竇憲干紀，無累安豐之祠；

translations.literal: In old times Dou Xian violated the statutes, yet the shrine of Anfeng was not implicated;
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Xian rebelled, the shrine of the Marquis of Anfeng was left untouched;

sentences.zh: 霍禹亂常，猶全博陸之祀。

translations.literal: Huo Yu disrupted the norm, yet the sacrifices of Bolu were still preserved in full.
translations.idiomatic: when Huo Yu disturbed the order of things, the sacrifices to Huo Guang were preserved.

sentences.zh: 罪不相及，國之通典。

translations.literal: Guilt does not extend to others — it is the nation's universal rule.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment does not extend to the innocent — that is a universal principle of state.

sentences.zh: 宜特垂恩禮，令所司速為起墳，所有官爵，並宜追復。

translations.literal: It is fitting specially to extend gracious rites, order the relevant offices promptly to rebuild the tomb, and all former ranks and titles should be posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: We should restore him to honor: let the proper offices rebuild his tomb at once, and restore all his ranks and titles.

sentences.zh: 」勣諸子孫坐敬業誅殺，靡有遺胤，偶脫禍者，皆竄跡胡越。

translations.literal: Ji's sons and grandsons, implicated through Jingye, were executed — none survived as heirs; those who by chance escaped calamity all fled and hid among the Hu and Yue barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's descendants were executed for Jingye's crime, and none survived. Those who by chance escaped fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 貞元十七年，吐蕃陷麟州，驅掠民畜而去。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan, Tibetans captured Lin Prefecture, drove off and plundered the people and livestock, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenyuan, the Tibetans took Lin Prefecture, seized people and livestock, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 至鹽州西橫槽烽，蕃將號徐舍人者，環集漢俘於呼延州，謂僧延素曰：「師勿甚懼，予本漢五代孫也。

translations.literal: Reaching Hengcao Beacon west of Yan Prefecture, the Tibetan general styled Vice Director Xu gathered Han captives in a ring at Huyanzhou and said to the monk Yansu, "Master, do not be greatly afraid — I am originally a fifth-generation descendant of Han."
translations.idiomatic: At Hengcao Beacon west of Yan Prefecture, a Tibetan officer known as Vice Director Xu gathered the Han captives at Huyanzhou and told the monk Yansu, "Do not be afraid, Master. I am a fifth-generation descendant of a Han family."

sentences.zh: 屬武太后斫喪王室，吾祖建義不果，子孫流落絕域，今三代矣。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu ruined and destroyed the royal house, my ancestor raised righteousness but did not succeed; descendants drifted to the borderlands — now three generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu wrecked the dynasty, my ancestor raised a revolt and failed. His line has lived in exile ever since — three generations now.

sentences.zh: 雖代居職任，掌握兵要，然思本之心，無忘於國。

translations.literal: Though for generations they have held office and duty and grasped military essentials, yet the heart thinking of origins has not forgotten the state.
translations.idiomatic: Though we hold office and command troops generation after generation, we have never forgotten our homeland.

sentences.zh: 但族屬已多，無由自拔耳。

translations.literal: Only the clan and kin are already numerous — there is no way to extricate oneself, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: But our clan is too large — there is no way for us to escape.

sentences.zh: 此地蕃漢交境，放師還鄉。

translations.literal: This place is where Tibetan and Han borders meet — I release the Master to return home."
translations.idiomatic: This is the border between Tibetan and Han lands. I release you to return home."

sentences.zh: 」數千百人，解縛而遣之。

translations.literal: Several thousand people — he unbound them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He freed and sent home several thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：近代稱為名將者，英、衛二公，誠煙閣之最。

translations.literal: The historian says: Among those called famous generals in recent times, the two Dukes of Ying and Wei truly are the foremost of the Smoke Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Among the great generals of recent times, the Dukes of Ying and Wei rank highest — the finest names on the merit rolls.

sentences.zh: 英公振彭、黥之跡，自拔草莽，常能以義籓身，與物無忤，遂得功名始終。

translations.literal: The Duke of Ying shook off the tracks of Peng and Qing, raised himself from grass and wilds, always able to use righteousness as a fence for the person, at odds with nothing — thus obtaining achievement and fame from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Ying cast off the path of bandit kings like Peng Yue and Qing Bu, rose from humble origins, lived by duty, harmed no one, and kept his fame intact to the end.

sentences.zh: 賢哉，垂命之誡！

translations.literal: How worthy — the dying injunction!
translations.idiomatic: How wise were his dying instructions!

sentences.zh: 敬業不蹈貽謀，至於覆族，悲夫！

translations.literal: Jingye did not tread in the counsel left behind — reaching the overturning of the clan — lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Jingye ignored that legacy and brought ruin on the whole clan — a tragedy!

sentences.zh: 衛公將家子，綽有渭陽之風。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wei, a general's house son, abundantly possessed the style of Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Wei came from a military family and bore something of the Wei clan's martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 臨戎出師，凜然威斷。

translations.literal: Facing battle and going forth with the army — stern and awe-inspiring in authority and decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he was formidable and resolute.

sentences.zh: 位重能避，功成益謙。

translations.literal: When rank was weighty he could withdraw; when achievement was complete he grew more modest.
translations.idiomatic: When power grew heavy he knew how to step aside; when success came he grew more humble.

sentences.zh: 銘之鼎鐘，何慚耿、鄧。

translations.literal: Inscribed on tripods and bells — what shame compared to Geng and Deng?
translations.idiomatic: Honors engraved on bronze and bell need not pale beside Geng and Deng.

sentences.zh: 美哉！

translations.literal: How beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Admirable indeed!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：功以懋賞，震主則危。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Merit receives lavish reward; when it awes the ruler, then there is danger.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: great merit earns great reward, but merit that overawes the throne brings peril.

sentences.zh: 辭祿避位，除猜破疑。

translations.literal: Declining emolument and avoiding position removes suspicion and breaks doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Declining rank and yielding place dispels envy and suspicion.

sentences.zh: 功定華夷，志懷忠義。

translations.literal: Achievement settled Hua and Yi; will embraced loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds pacified the realm; their hearts held fast to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 白首平戎，賢哉英、衛。

translations.literal: White-haired pacifying barbarians — worthy indeed, Duke of Ying and Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They fought on into old age — admirable, the Dukes of Ying and Wei.
